controls.title: Insurer-defined minimum security framework for agents, POSPs and individual surveyors
controls.prose: Insurance agents, micro-insurance agents, point of sale persons and individual surveyors are outside the direct purview of the Guidelines, but the insurer is responsible for ensuring these persons follow a minimum security framework defined in the insurer's Board-approved policy. The Guidelines apply to all data created, received or maintained by the regulated entity wherever it resides and in whatever form. Annexure I sets which NIST CSF sub-chapters (ID, PR, DE, RS, RC, WFRL) apply to each intermediary according to its access to the insurer's systems (view-only, API/EDI or processing, upload, storage, physical-only, or production support).
controls.guidance: Evidence the Board-approved minimum security framework for agents and POSPs (policy reference and Board resolution date in company-profile/<company_id>/summary.md) and how it is pushed to the agent onboarding app or POSP portal (MFA, device checks, data download limits). For each intermediary in company-profile/<company_id>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json record the Annexure I access category (a to f) in services[].description so probes know which sub-chapters to test. The Annexure I access category and the Annexure II gross-insurance-revenue category (Cat-1 >= Rs 50 crore or any ISNP or web aggregator, Cat-2 Rs 5 to 50 crore, Cat-3 < Rs 5 crore) have no reCategory slug yet, so control-level applicability cannot narrow by them; apply them manually when scoping. Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.4, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Board-approved minimum security framework for agents, micro-insurance agents, POSPs and individual surveyors
Annexure I access-category mapping for every intermediary engaged
Agent or POSP portal access controls enforcing the framework

controls.title: Information Security Risk Management Committee meets at least twice a year
controls.prose: The Information and Cyber Security Policy (ICSP) shall be governed by an Information Security Risk Management Committee (ISRMC) comprising the CRO, CISO, Chief IT Security Officer, CSO, CHRO, CTO and the function heads of Operations, Finance, Legal and Compliance. The ISRMC is responsible for changes to and approval of the policy and for keeping it updated at all times. An ISRMC meeting requires the CISO and at least two members, and all members shall meet at least twice a year. Implementation and enforcement of the ICSP is facilitated by the CISO and governed by the ISRMC. The ISRMC receives periodic inputs from the CISO and CITSO including security incidents with root cause and remediation, evaluates new initiatives from a security perspective, and gives periodic assurance to the Control Management Committee, which in turn reports to the Board.
controls.guidance: Collect ISRMC terms of reference, membership list and minutes for the last two half-years; check quorum (CISO plus two members), that the full committee met at least twice in the financial year, and that minutes cover incidents with RCA, exceptions, VAPT status and policy approvals. Record meeting dates as evidence on the soc control record and raise a finding when fewer than two full meetings are evidenced for the year (audit checklist Q117).
evidenceExpected: ISRMC charter with named members
Minutes of at least two full-committee meetings per year showing quorum
Incident, RCA and remediation packs tabled to the ISRMC
Periodic assurance note from ISRMC to the Control Management Committee

params.label: Minimum meetings of all ISRMC members per year

controls.title: Annual ICSP review by CISO with ISRMC approval
controls.prose: The ICSP is owned by the CISO and maintained by the Information Security team; the CRO assumes CISO responsibilities for decisions in the CISO's absence. The policy shall be reviewed annually and updated where required by the CISO and approved by the ISRMC, considering changes in regulation, industry standards, new business operations, new channels, new technologies, HR policy changes and incidents inside or outside the organisation. Renewals and changes shall be notified to all employees through email, intranet, annual refresher training or similar means.
controls.guidance: Evidence the current ICSP version, its approval date by the ISRMC and Board, the review log showing each trigger was considered, and the employee communication. Flag a finding when the last approved review is older than twelve months. Link the policy reference in company-profile/<company_id>/summary.md regulatory posture section (audit checklist Q128, Q119 to Q122).
evidenceExpected: Current Board-approved ICSP with version history
ISRMC approval of the annual review
Review checklist covering regulatory, technology, business and incident triggers
Employee notification of policy changes

controls.title: Board accountability, CISO appointment and quarterly security inputs
controls.prose: The Board of Directors shall play a proactive role in information and cyber security governance and is ultimately responsible for the information security of the organisation. The Board shall approve the appointment of the CISO, receive quarterly inputs on information security matters, approve the Information and Cyber Security Policy and approve and review the IT framework. The Board shall provide appropriate resources and budget, and commitment of senior management shall be ensured. The audit checklist additionally expects an internal technology committee that periodically reviews policy implementation, IT architecture review by the IT sub-committee of the Board, and cyber risk training for all Board members at least once a year.
controls.guidance: Collect Board and Board Risk Management Committee agendas and minutes for the last four quarters showing an information security agenda item, the Board resolution approving the CISO appointment and the ICSP, and records of annual Board cyber training (checklist Q131, Q132, Q134, Q235). A missing quarter is a finding. Store dates as soc observations under refresh-soc; report-audit-findings summarises Board oversight in the regulatory posture section.
evidenceExpected: Board resolution approving CISO appointment and ICSP
Quarterly Board or Board-committee minutes with information security updates
Record of annual cyber security training for all Board members
Internal technology committee review of cyber security policy implementation

controls.title: Senior, independent CISO with defined security standards
controls.prose: A sufficiently senior official with requisite technical background and expertise shall be designated CISO. The CISO should have a reasonable minimum term and should report directly to the top executive overseeing risk management or, in that person's absence, to the CEO, and shall assume overall responsibility for governance and monitoring of information security. The CISO defines and periodically reviews the ICSP and IS standards (technology risk assessment methodology, BCP/DR and BIA standards, application security and vendor risk standards, training standards, vendor classification and VAPT baselines), conducts and coordinates internal and external IS reviews, briefs the ISRMC, approves exceptions, oversees closure of incidents and escalates incidents open beyond SLA to the CRO and ISRMC, and is responsible for reporting critical or high severity incidents to regulators.
controls.guidance: Check company-profile/<company_id>/details.json contacts for a CISO entry, the appointment letter and organisation chart showing the reporting line to the CRO or CEO (not to the CTO or CIO), and the published set of IS standards with owners and review dates. Raise a high finding when the CISO reports into IT delivery or the role is vacant or combined with the CTO. Checklist Q116.
evidenceExpected: CISO appointment letter and organisation chart with reporting line
Catalogue of IS standards owned by the CISO (TRA, VAPT baseline, vendor classification, training, BCP/DR)
Escalation records of incidents breaching SLA to CRO and ISRMC

controls.title: IT Security Operations: 24x7 SOC, LAM, DLP and TRA sub-teams
controls.prose: An IT Security Operations team reporting to the Chief IT Security Officer shall run sub-teams for the Security Operations Centre, Logical Access Management, Data Leakage Prevention and Technology Risk Assessment, with all incident reporting routed through the CISO. The SOC performs real-time monitoring, first-level analysis and false-positive triage, reports incidents to the CISO and IS team and tracks them to closure; logs of application and IT infrastructure shall be collected and analysed by a 24x7 SOC. LAM provisions, modifies and revokes access per the access control matrix and runs periodic user re-certification with business owners. DLP implements leakage prevention per the classification standard and reports leakage incidents to the CISO. TRA is performed before any new or changed process or technology, with CISO approval where required. The CITSO oversees these tools and ensures incidents detected by them reach the CISO.
controls.guidance: Evidence the operating model: SOC roster or MSSP contract showing 24x7 coverage, SIEM log-source inventory against the asset inventory (every production environment in applications/<app_id>/env/<env_id>.json should have observability.siem set), LAM recertification campaign records, DLP policy coverage and TRA register. runtime-probe-prod-env verifies log forwarding from workloads; refresh-vendor-ctx covers an outsourced SOC. Checklist Q84, Q126.
evidenceExpected: 24x7 SOC roster or managed SOC contract with SLAs
SIEM log-source coverage report against the asset inventory
User access recertification campaign results
DLP policy and incident reports to the CISO
Technology Risk Assessment register

controls.title: Internal audit independent assessment of information security
controls.prose: The internal audit function shall provide an independent review of the organisation's information security initiatives and objective assurance to the Board and executive management on how effectively IS risks are assessed and managed, including the effectiveness of IT Security Operations and the IS risk management structure. It shall keep the Audit Committee apprised of emerging risks, identify weaknesses in policies and controls, and independently assess key IS risks, the controls management has put in place, whether functional managers use them and whether they operate effectively.
controls.guidance: Collect the internal audit plan showing information security scope, the latest IS internal audit report and its presentation to the Audit Committee, and the tracker of findings. Import open internal audit observations as soc findings so their closure is tracked with the rest of the ledger.
evidenceExpected: Internal audit plan with information security scope
Internal audit report on IS and Audit Committee minutes
Tracker of internal audit IS findings

controls.title: Information security risk assessment at least annually and before key changes
controls.prose: The organisation shall perform risk assessment at least annually and before introducing major new technologies or initiatives, using external service providers (outsourcing, offshoring or cloud), permitting external individuals to access critical systems, and granting access from external locations. Risk assessment covers business environments, processes, applications (including those in development), information systems and networks, specialist systems and people including third-party vendors, and applies early in development, before significant changes and when outsourcing is considered. Reviews shall verify the adequacy of existing controls, residual and acceptable risk, measure control effectiveness and identify new risks from significant changes.
controls.guidance: Evidence the annual IS risk assessment report with methodology, risk register and approval date, plus trigger-based assessments for new cloud onboarding, vendor onboarding and remote access programmes in the last year. Maxwell cross-checks that each vendor in vendors/<vendor_id>.json with lastAssessment and each new application in applications/ has a risk assessment dated before go-live. Checklist Q135, Q138, Q139, Q140. The registry hardRequirements cite the annual risk assessment obligation as section "1.8"; this is the control that carries it.
evidenceExpected: Annual information security risk assessment report and methodology
Risk register with owners, ratings and treatment status
Trigger-based assessments for outsourcing, cloud and external access decisions
Documented organisational risk tolerance

controls.title: Technology Risk Assessment with residual risk sign-off by the right owner
controls.prose: The IS team shall define technology risk assessment templates or checklists whose output identifies the risks from a new technology, process or change, the mitigating controls selected from a reputable control framework, and the residual risk classified as financial, operational, regulatory or technology. Residual risks shall be approved by the defined owners: financial by the CFO, operational by the COO and business process owner, enterprise or information security by the CISO or CRO, regulatory by the CRO and technology by the CTO. Treatment actions and residual risk shall be recorded in a risk treatment plan signed off by the owner and at least one executive, and signed-off risks shall be periodically reviewed by the IS team.
controls.guidance: Sample change requests and new initiatives from change_management/master.json and verify a TRA exists with residual risk category and sign-off by the owner the Guidelines name. impl-change-management should attach the TRA reference to initiative tasks before approval. A risk accepted by the wrong authority is a finding.
evidenceExpected: TRA templates and checklists approved by the IS team
Completed TRAs for sampled changes with residual risk classification
Risk treatment plans signed by risk owner and an executive

controls.title: Documented, risk-assessed and time-bound policy exceptions
controls.prose: Exceptions to the information and cyber security policies shall be decided at senior management level on a case-by-case basis on the information owner's request, after a technology risk assessment and approvals per the risk management process. Every exception shall be documented and retained by the IS team for as long as it exists, recording the value and sensitivity of the asset, the policy excepted, the risk and exposure, acceptance of that risk, the business reason, compensating controls and the actions and schedule to reach compliance; where corrective action is planned, its time frame should be identified and the actions should be tracked to closure. During emergencies such as pandemics or natural disasters a Crisis Management Committee shall approve workaround processes on collated risks, with ratification by the Board Risk Management Committee, and compromises shall be eliminated once normalcy returns.
controls.guidance: Maxwell records accepted exceptions as soc risk records with acceptedBy and acceptedUntil; flag any exception without an expiry, compensating controls or approver of the required seniority, and any accepted risk past acceptedUntil. Collect the exception register and a sample of approvals. Checklist Q1 expects a Board-approved exception policy for insurers and Cat-1 intermediaries and MD approval for Cat-2 and Cat-3.
evidenceExpected: Exception policy approved by the Board (or MD for smaller intermediaries)
Exception register with risk, compensating controls, approver and expiry
Crisis Management Committee decisions and Board RMC ratification for emergency exceptions

controls.title: Annual independent assurance audit presented to the Audit Committee or Board
controls.prose: An independent assurance audit against the Guidelines shall be carried out by an eligible auditor every year, and the annual audit plan and reports shall be presented to the Audit Committee, Board of Directors or Principal Officer as applicable. The auditor's report follows Annexure III (summary, overall status of findings by NIST CSF area, details of non-compliances with High, Medium or Low risk rating, and the audit checklist) and is certified using the Annexure V text. Entities that had completed their FY 2022-23 security audit were to comply from the next financial year.
controls.guidance: Record the audit period, auditor name and report date in company-profile/<company_id>/details.json (auditCadence, lastCyberAuditAt). Collect the Annexure III report, Annexure V certificate and Audit Committee minutes. Import each Part C non-compliance as a soc finding citing irdai-info-cyber-security-2023 and the checklist question in location, keeping the auditor's risk rating as severity. Checklist Q118. The registry hardRequirements cite this annual audit obligation as section "1.10". Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Annexure III auditor report for the financial year
Annexure V (or VI for FRBs) audit certificate
Audit Committee or Board minutes presenting the audit plan and report
Tracker of audit non-compliances with closure status

controls.title: Insurer submits Annexure III audit report to IRDAI within 90 days of FY end or 30 days of audit
controls.prose: Insurers shall submit their audit report in the Annexure III format, duly signed by the auditor and with the comments of the Board, to IRDAI within 90 days from the end of the financial year or within 30 days of completion of the audit, whichever is earlier.
controls.guidance: Track the submission as a dated observation: the due date is min(FY end + 90 days, audit completion + 30 days), computed from details.json fiscalYearStart and lastCyberAuditAt with params submissionDaysAfterFyEnd and submissionDaysAfterAudit; for a 31 March year end the 90-day leg ends on 29 June. No slaDays: both numbers are a reporting deadline, not a window to remediate a gap, so a finding against this control takes its deadline from the SLA table by severity. Evidence the IRDAI submission acknowledgement and the Board comments annexed. The registry hardRequirements cite this obligation as section "1.10". Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Auditor-signed Annexure III report with Board comments
IRDAI submission acknowledgement with date
Computation of the earlier of FY end + 90 days and audit completion + 30 days

params.label: Days after financial year end for submission to IRDAI
Days after completion of audit for submission to IRDAI, whichever is earlier

controls.title: Intermediary submits Annexure III with Board comments to each insurer annually
controls.prose: Insurance intermediaries shall submit the Annexure III audit report, together with compliance thereto and the comments of their Board, to the insurer or insurers they work with every year.
controls.guidance: For intermediary companies, evidence the dated transmittal of the Annexure III report to every insurer partner listed in details.json regulatoryRegistrations or partner contracts, with Board comments attached. Missing transmittal to any active insurer partner is a finding. Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Annexure III report with compliance status and Board comments
Transmittal records to each insurer partner

controls.title: Insurer oversight of intermediaries' compliance under a Board-approved policy
controls.prose: Insurers shall ensure that the insurance intermediaries they engage comply with the Guidelines during the engagement, under a Board-approved policy that also sets the maximum Part C audit risk rating acceptable for entering into or continuing business with an intermediary. For intermediaries that retain only insurer data in physical form and neither hold an electronic database of insurer data nor access insurer systems, the insurer shall obtain self-certifications annually before entering into or continuing business.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx maintains one vendors/<vendor_id>.json per intermediary with assurance entries for the latest Annexure III report or self-certificate and its expiry; flag intermediaries without current assurance or whose Part C rating exceeds the Board threshold. Evidence the Board-approved intermediary cyber policy and the threshold value. Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Board-approved policy on intermediary cyber security compliance with maximum risk rating
Annexure III reports received from each electronically connected intermediary
Annual self-certifications from physical-data-only intermediaries

params.label: Maximum Part C risk rating for entering into or continuing business with an intermediary, per Board policy

controls.title: FRB certificate under Annexure VI submitted to IRDAI every financial year
controls.prose: Foreign Reinsurance Branches whose IT systems are interfaced with their overseas parent companies shall comply with the cyber security Guidelines; the auditor shall certify compliance in the Annexure VI format and the certificate shall be submitted to IRDAI at the end of every financial year.
controls.guidance: Applies only where details.json identifies the company as a Foreign Reinsurance Branch. Evidence the Annexure VI certificate, its Annexure A summary of compliant, non-compliant and not-applicable controls, and IRDAI submission proof. Interfaces with the parent group should appear in vendors/ as intraGroup services. Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: Annexure VI auditor certificate for the FRB
IRDAI submission acknowledgement
Inventory of IT interfaces with the overseas parent

controls.title: Adhere to CERT-In directions and applicable laws
controls.prose: Regulated entities shall adhere to directions issued by CERT-In from time to time on information security practices, procedures, prevention, response and reporting of cyber incidents, and shall ensure compliance with each law and act relevant to their operations, including the Information Technology Act and IRDAI regulations.
controls.guidance: Treat cert-in-directions-2022 as in scope for every IRDAI regulated entity: add it to details.json frameworksInScope and evaluate its catalog controls (NTP sync, 6-hour reporting, 180-day logs in India, point of contact). This control is satisfied when the CERT-In controls in the soc ledger are implemented; a gap in any mapped CERT-In control is a gap here. Id note: the printed section has unnumbered paragraphs, so the letter suffix in this id was assigned during extraction; quote the source as "section 1.10, paragraph beginning ..." and cite this id in regulatoryRefs.
evidenceExpected: CERT-In directions listed in the compliance register with owners
soc control records for each CERT-In direction
CERT-In point of contact registration

controls.title: Four-level data classification with PII tagging and biennial owner review
controls.prose: Every information asset shall have a designated owner who classifies it as Confidential, Restricted, Internal Use Only or Public according to its relative risk, value and sensitivity; unlabelled information is treated as Internal Use Only at a minimum. Personally identifiable information shall additionally be identified and classified as PII (sensitive personal information or other personal information) and protected with reasonable safeguards. Owners remain accountable when delegating, and shall review assigned classification labels at least every two years or when laws and regulations require.
controls.guidance: refresh-metastore and probe-schemas compare column-level dataClassification and pii flags in company-profile/<company_id>/sdlc/metastore.json against the four IRDAI levels (map confidential and restricted to the metastore's highest tiers) and flag unclassified tables holding policyholder, claims, KYC, health or bank data. Evidence the classification standard, the data owner register and the last review date per data domain.
evidenceExpected: Data classification standard with the four IRDAI levels and PII categories
Data owner register
Metastore classification coverage report for production data stores
Classification review records not older than two years

params.label: Maximum interval between owner reviews of classification labels

controls.title: Lifecycle handling of Confidential and Restricted information
controls.prose: Confidential and Restricted information shall be labelled, stored only on company-owned or controlled systems (or equivalently secured approved partners) that uniquely authenticate every user and are periodically reviewed and monitored, and transmitted outside the organisation's network only in encrypted form or over a secured channel with keys managed under the cryptographic policy. Tracking shall record who accessed the information, from where (MAC or IP address) and when, and the owner shall audit that access and correct deficiencies. Such information and all copies and backups shall be securely destroyed at the end of the retention period or release of a litigation or audit hold, and sensitive systems not regularly accessed shall be removed from the network.
controls.guidance: probe-iac and probe-app-chart check storage encryption, TLS-only ingress and object-store public access for datasets classified confidential or restricted; runtime-probe-datapipeline verifies data-access audit logs capture principal, source IP and timestamp for those datasets and that retentionDays is set in the metastore. Findings: unencrypted egress of confidential data, missing access logs, confidential data on unapproved SaaS.
evidenceExpected: Encryption in transit and at rest configuration for stores holding Confidential or Restricted data
Data access audit logs showing user, source address and time
Owner access audit records
Retention schedule and secure destruction records

controls.title: Protect policyholder and employee personal data through its lifecycle
controls.prose: Sensitive personal data (passwords, financial and payment instrument details, physical and mental health conditions, medical records, biometrics, call data records and similar) shall be protected as Confidential and other personal information as Restricted. Consent shall be obtained on the purpose and means of use before collection; sensitive personal information shall be collected only for a lawful purpose and where necessary, individuals shall be told of the collection, purpose and recipients, data shall be used only for its purpose and not kept longer than required, and individuals may review and correct their data. Access shall be strictly need-to-know, disclosure outside the organisation limited to consent, regulators and auditors, legal requirement, service providers to the individual and fraud prevention agencies, privacy incidents reported immediately, and data protection tools such as DLP and digital rights management implemented.
controls.guidance: Treat this as the IRDAI hook for DPDP obligations: evaluate dpdp-rules-2025 controls for notice, safeguards and erasure alongside it. probe-schemas and refresh-metastore locate health, bank and Aadhaar fields in claims, underwriting and KYC stores and check masking, tokenisation and retention; runtime-probe-datapipeline checks that analytics copies of health data are masked. Evidence consent capture in proposal journeys and DLP policy coverage for email and endpoints.
evidenceExpected: Inventory of SPI and OPI data elements with storage locations
Consent and notice records in proposal and claims journeys
DLP and DRM policies covering SPI
Retention and erasure evidence for personal data
Data disclosure register

controls.title: Comprehensive, current asset inventory and CMDB including unsupported software
controls.prose: A comprehensive, accurate and up-to-date inventory of all information assets shall be maintained, recording at a minimum identification, description, location, owner, custodian, business value, classification and its validity, support information, AMC details for hardware and licence details for software, with enough information to recover from a disaster. Software inventory tools shall automate documentation of all software on business systems; only vendor-supported software shall be added to the authorised software inventory and unsupported software tagged. Configuration items shall be defined, classified, tracked from ordering to depreciation and held with their relationships in a configuration management database whose changes are controlled. Unauthorised assets shall be removed, quarantined or inventoried promptly.
controls.guidance: Maxwell's applications/<app_id>/ env, repos and images files plus the metastore are the machine inventory; probe-iac and probe-app-chart reconcile declared cloud resources and workloads against them, runtime-probe-prod-env lists running workloads and nodes not in the inventory, and probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers flag end-of-life base images and runtimes (checklist Q106, Q107, Q111, Q200, Q201). Evidence the CMDB export and software inventory tool coverage.
evidenceExpected: CMDB or asset register export with mandatory fields populated
Automated software inventory report with unsupported software tagged
Reconciliation of cloud and Kubernetes resources to the inventory
Records of removal or quarantine of unauthorised assets

controls.title: Only authorised devices connect: certificates, 802.1x and inventory-linked NAC
controls.prose: The asset inventory shall record the authorisation mechanism for every asset: for organisation-owned devices the owner and the identifier used to admit them to the network (MAC address or IMEI), and for non-owned devices the two-factor authentication parameters. Insurers shall use client certificates to authenticate hardware connecting to the trusted network, port-level access control following 802.1x shall control which devices can authenticate, and the authentication system shall be tied to the hardware inventory so only authorised devices connect.
controls.guidance: Evidence NAC or 802.1x configuration, device certificate issuance from the corporate PKI or MDM, and a report of blocked unknown devices. For cloud-first estates, runtime-probe-identity-access checks device-trust conditions (managed-device or certificate-based conditional access) on the identity provider and VPN or ZTNA gateway. Checklist Q87, Q102 to Q104.
evidenceExpected: 802.1x or NAC policy tied to the hardware inventory
Device certificate issuance records
Conditional access or ZTNA device-trust policy
Log of blocked unauthorised device connections

controls.title: Secure disposal, removable media handling and asset return
controls.prose: Assets and media holding critical or sensitive information shall be disposed of securely by incineration, shredding or approved erasure, with data removed before disposal, critical infrastructure disposal approved by the CTO and CFO, and a register of disposed assets kept; damaged devices with sensitive data require a risk assessment on destruction versus repair. Removable media shall be listed, stored securely, authorised and logged when removed, and confidential data on it encrypted; hard drives shall be removed or wiped before hardware goes to maintenance vendors. All assets shall be returned on termination.
controls.guidance: Evidence the disposal register with certificates of destruction, removable media policy with USB encryption or blocking via endpoint management, and asset return records at exit. For cloud, check that decommissioned volumes and snapshots are deleted (probe-iac: orphaned encrypted volumes and public snapshots) (checklist Q44, Q178). Id note: in the PDF the 3.2.4 to 3.2.7 headings of policy 2.2 are separated from their text, so this control merges the asset disposal clause (3.2.6) with the adjoining transfer of physical media, return of assets and removable media clauses of the same 3.2 block; loss or theft of assets (printed 3.3) is 2.2-3.3.
evidenceExpected: Register of disposed or scrapped assets with destruction certificates
Removable media inventory and encryption or block policy
Courier and transit logs for physical media
Asset return records at exit

controls.title: Report loss or theft of devices immediately, revoke access and remote wipe
controls.prose: In case of loss or theft of a personal device with access to the organisation's information assets, the employee shall report it immediately. The IT function shall immediately revoke all access to information assets through the device and attempt to remotely wipe organisation data from it. If the loss or theft is reported after more than 4 hours, or the remote wipe is unsuccessful, it shall be recorded as an incident and handled under the incident management procedure.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks MDM or endpoint management for remote wipe capability and wipe logs, and that the identity provider revokes sessions and device tokens for devices marked lost. Compare lost-device tickets with incident records: a loss reported more than 4 hours after it occurred, or a failed wipe, without a soc incident is a finding (checklist Q180; 2.7-3.1 and 2.8-3.7.2 carry the mobile and BYOD equivalents).
evidenceExpected: Lost or stolen device tickets with report times
Access revocation and remote wipe logs
Incident records for late reports or failed wipes

params.label: Hours after which a late-reported device loss is recorded as an incident

controls.title: Unique accountable user IDs; generic and group IDs only by exception
controls.prose: Each user or process shall have a unique User-ID for which the individual is accountable; IDs are non-transferable, shared use is forbidden and individuals shall not hold multiple accounts in the same environment. Generic and group IDs shall be avoided and, where unavoidable, created only through the exception process with a named accountable owner, short-term use and an expiry date. Where individual IDs are technically impossible, alternative means of restricting and auditing access shall be implemented.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access lists identity provider, cloud IAM, database and Kubernetes accounts, flags shared or generic accounts (admin, ops, test, service users used interactively), duplicate accounts per person and generic accounts without owner tags or expiry. Evidence the exception approvals for each generic ID.
evidenceExpected: Account inventory per system mapped to named individuals
Exception approvals, owners and expiry for generic or group IDs
Evidence of interactive use restrictions on service accounts

controls.title: HR-triggered joiner, mover and leaver access with password standard
controls.prose: Network and system access shall be granted only on intimation from HR through a formal registration process with approval of access rights, and revoked through a formal de-registration process triggered by HR with confirmation returned for exit clearance. Access shall enforce segregation of duties and need-to-know, and on transfer the previous role's access shall be revoked. Initial passwords shall be delivered securely and changed at first logon, passwords changed every 45 days, previous passwords remembered to prevent reuse, passwords encrypted in storage and transit with password files stored separately, and administrative passwords for critical systems managed under defined procedures. Department heads shall periodically review and centrally record access rights.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access compares the identity provider and critical application user lists to the HR leaver feed (request via task if unavailable) and flags active accounts of leavers, users with access from previous roles, and password policies weaker than the IRDAI standard. Where the company uses phishing-resistant MFA and no periodic rotation, record the deviation as an approved exception rather than silently passing. Checklist Q149, Q150, Q172 to Q174. The registry hardRequirements cite the 45-day password change as policy "2.3"; this is the control that carries it (param passwordMaxAgeDays).
evidenceExpected: Access request and approval records linked to HR joiner tickets
Leaver reconciliation showing revocation dates against exit dates
Password policy configuration (first-logon change, 45-day expiry, history)
Periodic access review sign-offs by department heads

params.label: Maximum password age before users must change it

controls.title: Independent layered authorisation with MFA from non-organisation devices and networks
controls.prose: Users shall be authorised independently at the physical, network, infrastructure, endpoint, application and cloud levels, authenticated by a domain policy server, with applications integrating with the enterprise identity management system. Single-factor authentication suffices only for requests from organisation-owned devices and networks; two-factor authentication is mandatory from non-organisation devices or networks, and cloud-hosted applications shall accept an authorisation validated by an organisation-owned authorisation service or require two-factor authentication. Critical systems reachable over the internet shall have two-factor security. Users shall re-authenticate after inactivity, an emergency access process shall exist, and methods shall prevent unauthorised access to individual and departmental shared files.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access verifies SSO federation for SaaS and internal apps, conditional-access rules requiring MFA off-network, MFA enforcement on cloud consoles, VPN and customer or partner portals, idle session timeouts and a break-glass procedure with alerting. probe-app-chart and execute-scr check that applications delegate authentication to the enterprise IdP rather than local user tables. Checklist Q64, Q65, Q148, Q176.
evidenceExpected: Identity provider conditional-access policies requiring MFA from unmanaged devices or networks
SSO integration inventory for applications and cloud services
Session timeout configuration
Emergency (break-glass) access procedure and usage logs

controls.title: Privileged accounts minimised, justified, logged and never shared
controls.prose: Privileges for operating systems, applications, databases and network elements shall be identified and documented, and privileged accounts limited to individuals with business justification and the required skills, allocated need-to-have under an authorisation process with a record of all privileges. Use of privileged IDs shall be minimised, separate logons used for privileged and routine work where feasible, all privileged activity securely logged and reviewed, sharing of privileged IDs and credentials prohibited, and vendor or contractor privileged access allowed only under close supervision with documented justification. Privileged users shall be restricted from accessing the logs that capture their own activity, privileged authorisations reviewed more frequently, and rules for software installation by users enforced.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access enumerates cloud owner and admin roles, Kubernetes cluster-admin bindings, database superusers and IdP global admins; flags standing privileged access without PAM or just-in-time elevation, shared root or admin credentials, vendor principals with admin rights and admins able to delete audit logs. probe-iac flags wildcard IAM policies. Checklist Q151, Q274.
evidenceExpected: Privileged account inventory with justification and approver
PAM or just-in-time elevation configuration and session recordings
Privileged activity log reviews
Controls preventing privileged users from altering their own audit logs

controls.title: Secure log-on, lockout and periodic access rights review
controls.prose: The log-on process shall reveal nothing that aids an unauthorised user, validate data only once fully entered without indicating which part is wrong, enforce account lockout after the retry limit, display a warning notice, log successful and unsuccessful attempts, never transmit passwords in clear text and terminate inactive sessions. User access rights shall be reviewed at regular intervals and after promotion, demotion, role change or termination, privileged authorisations shall be reviewed more frequently with changes logged, and privilege allocations checked for unauthorised privileges. Dormant, orphan and redundant accounts shall be detected and suspended, not reissued, and attempts to access deactivated accounts logged.
controls.guidance: execute-scr and runtime-probe-identity-access test lockout thresholds, generic error messages and login-attempt logging on customer, agent and admin portals; runtime-probe-identity-access reports dormant accounts beyond the policy inactivity threshold and the date of the last access review campaign per critical application. Checklist Q10, Q26, Q54, Q157.
evidenceExpected: Lockout and session timeout configuration
Login success and failure logs
Access review campaign records including privileged access
Dormant and orphan account reports with suspension actions

controls.title: Remote access on need basis with approvals, 15-day third-party ID expiry and monthly account review
controls.prose: Remote access for employees, vendors and contractors shall be granted only on need-to-know and need-to-do basis; third-party remote access requests shall be raised by the responsible employee with business justification and approved by the sponsoring manager, Head of IT and Group CISO, with an exception where access is from non-organisation endpoints. Remote access software use shall be restricted, no vendor or general user shall hold administrative rights on the SSL VPN appliance, third-party privileged activity shall be monitored and revoked on termination, and third-party User-IDs shall expire in not more than 15 days unless approved. Remote access shall use strong end-to-end encryption over a secure channel without circumventing security controls. Evidence of grants, revocations, configuration changes and patching of remote access systems shall be kept, and system owners shall verify monthly that active remote access accounts are accurate.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access and runtime-probe-network-perimeter check VPN or ZTNA configuration (TLS versions, MFA, split tunnelling), vendor accounts older than 15 days without renewal approval, VPN admin role holders and patch level of the VPN appliance against known exploited CVEs (cve-enrichment). Evidence the monthly remote-access account reconciliation.
evidenceExpected: Remote access approvals by sponsor, Head of IT and Group CISO for third parties
Third-party remote account expiry configuration (15 days)
Monthly reconciliation of active remote access accounts
VPN or ZTNA configuration and patch records

params.label: Maximum validity of third-party user IDs before re-approval

controls.title: Restricted and logged access to program source code
controls.prose: Access to program source code and associated items such as designs and test plans shall be strictly controlled to prevent unauthorised functionality or changes and protect intellectual property. Source libraries shall not be held on operational systems and shall be managed under established procedures, IT support staff shall not have unrestricted access, updates and issue of sources shall require authorisation, and an audit log of all access to source libraries shall be maintained.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc and probe-cicd-env inspect the source control organisation: SSO and MFA enforced, least-privilege repository roles, branch protection per sdlc/policy.json, audit log streaming, no source code or .git directories in production images (runtime-probe-appcontainers) and no broad access for support or vendor accounts.
evidenceExpected: Source control access list with roles and MFA enforcement
Branch protection and code review settings
Source control audit log export
Evidence that production hosts and images do not contain source libraries

controls.title: Background verification and security terms before and during employment
controls.prose: Job roles shall document general and specific security responsibilities. Background checks shall be performed on all personnel, including temporary and contract staff, in sensitive or critical roles before selection or transfer, third-party personnel shall be background-checked by their employers with assurance given, and information given at recruitment verified. Employees, contractors and third-party users shall sign contracts with confidentiality or non-disclosure terms stating security responsibilities, be briefed before access to confidential information, and be subject to a documented disciplinary process for breaches. Job rotation shall apply to computer-related positions of trust, dependency on single persons avoided through succession plans, users leaving the company monitored more closely, and an anonymous channel provided to report policy violations.
controls.guidance: Sample HR files for engineers, SOC staff and database administrators and verify background verification completion before access grant date; for vendors, collect assurance letters stored under vendors/<vendor_id>.json assurance. Evidence signed NDAs, disciplinary policy and whistle-blower or anonymous reporting channel.
evidenceExpected: Background verification reports dated before access provisioning for sensitive roles
Signed NDAs or confidentiality clauses
Vendor assurance of background checks for outsourced staff
Disciplinary process and anonymous reporting channel

controls.title: Security awareness programme with tracked attendance and cyber exercises
controls.prose: Information security training and awareness shall be provided to all employees, contractors and relevant third-party users, with a programme defining content, timeline and periodicity. Attendance shall be tracked, non-attendees given a stipulated time after which it is a policy non-compliance, and history and versions of training content maintained. Additional training shall be provided to leaders on their roles in a security incident, secure coding training to developers, periodic dos and don'ts communicated, and the organisation shall periodically participate in national, sectoral or organisational cyber security exercises. The audit checklist expects the awareness programme to be updated at least annually and awareness levels evaluated.
controls.guidance: Collect LMS completion reports for the last cycle with the non-completion escalation, phishing simulation results, secure coding training for engineers (checklist Q34) and evidence of participation in CERT-In or sectoral drills (Q169). Completion below the policy target or no exercise participation in the year is a finding.
evidenceExpected: Training programme with periodicity and versioned content
LMS completion and escalation reports
Incident-role training records for leaders
Certificates or reports of participation in cyber security exercises

controls.title: Orderly exit with immediate removal of physical and logical access
controls.prose: Termination of employees, contractors and third-party users shall be orderly with defined responsibilities. Assets shall be returned and all physical and logical access removed immediately; mechanisms shall revoke access before the end of employment or contract, and detect and act immediately on any failure to remove access. Access shall be reassessed on change of role or transfer, and any security violations during tenure reviewed before final sign-off.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access reconciles leaver dates from HR against last-disabled timestamps in the IdP, VPN, cloud IAM, source control and privileged applications and raises a finding for any account active after the exit date. Evidence the exit checklist and physical badge deactivation logs.
evidenceExpected: Exit checklists with asset return and access revocation dates
Leaver-to-account reconciliation report
Badge deactivation logs
Detection alerts for access by terminated users

controls.title: Minimum Baseline Security Standards and hardening before production
controls.prose: Security requirements shall be identified, justified and agreed with business owners during requirements analysis for acquisition, development or change, reflecting the business value of the information. Minimum Baseline Security Standards (MBSS) shall be developed and maintained covering both data protection and the system software, and every information system (servers, routers, firewalls and similar) shall be hardened to the MBSS before commissioning in production. Clocks of relevant systems shall be synchronised with an agreed accurate time source. Critical systems shall be designed for high availability with fault-tolerant configuration and availability monitoring.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks Terraform or CloudFormation against CIS benchmark-derived MBSS (encryption, public exposure, IMDSv2, logging), probe-app-chart checks Helm values for pod security (non-root, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, resource limits), and runtime-probe-appcontainers and runtime-probe-prod-env check running workloads for drift from the baseline. Evidence the documented MBSS per platform and the pre-production hardening sign-off (checklist Q42, Q216).
evidenceExpected: MBSS documents per operating system, database, container platform, cloud and network device
Hardening compliance scan results before go-live
Configuration drift reports for production
High-availability design for critical systems

controls.title: Secure development framework and application security review before production
controls.prose: Applications shall pass a security review against IS-team application security standards before production. The IS team shall build a software development security framework with a software risk assessment process and a library of secure design patterns whose use is enforced; vendor packages shall be used with minimum modification and all modifications made under formal program change control. For third-party developed software the organisation shall ensure the vendor's process complies with its policy, obtain licensing, quality and documentation commitments, source code ownership or escrow, a contractual right to audit development processes, and acceptance testing including security, and shall set security thresholds for minimum acceptable security and privacy quality. Applications shall validate input and output, protect message integrity, and block unapproved software by central policy. Security-critical code shall be identified and checked for known weaknesses.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc checks sdlc/policy.json ciGates for SAST, SCA and secret scanning with blocking thresholds and that they run on every repo in applications/<app_id>/repos/; execute-scr performs secure code review on critical applications (proposal, policy administration, claims, payment callback) for input validation and authorisation flaws; probe-cicd-env confirms gates cannot be bypassed. For vendor-built core systems, evidence the escrow agreement and right-to-audit clause via refresh-vendor-ctx (checklist Q8, Q41, Q43, Q57).
evidenceExpected: Secure SDLC framework and secure design pattern library
Application security review sign-off before each production release of critical applications
SAST, SCA and secret scanning results enforced in CI
Source code escrow or ownership clause and right to audit for vendor-built software

controls.title: Security architecture review and independent security acceptance testing
controls.prose: The technical and functional architecture of any new information system shall be reviewed and approved by the IS team, and its interdependencies with the overall environment assessed from a security perspective; operating platform changes shall trigger review of application controls and business continuity plans. New and updated systems shall be thoroughly tested with a planned schedule, inputs and expected outputs; development teams test first and independent acceptance testing follows for both in-house and outsourced development, covering security requirements and secure development practices, on received components and integrated systems, in a realistic test environment. Use of operational data containing PII or other confidential information for testing shall be avoided.
controls.guidance: Link each production application to an architecture review record in change_management initiatives; probe-agent-graph covers architecture review of AI agent and LLM components; runtime-probe-qa-env and runtime-probe-devtest-env sample non-production databases for unmasked policyholder PII or health data, which is a high finding. Evidence UAT and security test sign-offs.
evidenceExpected: IS team architecture review approvals for new systems
Independent acceptance test reports including security test cases
Test data management procedure with masking of production PII
Non-production data sampling results

controls.title: Encrypted backups with restoration testing at least every six months
controls.prose: Backup frequency, restoration testing frequency and storage requirements shall be defined by data classification in an IS-team backup and restoration standard, with data restoration testing performed at a minimum every six months or more often as the business requires. Applications, operating systems, databases, configurations and required logs shall be identified for backup with medium and offsite location documented. All backup media shall be encrypted, restores logged, additional backups taken before configuration changes and upgrades, tape movements recorded, restoration tested onto dedicated test media rather than overwriting originals, backup execution monitored and failures addressed, website content backed up, and retention for essential information defined. The audit checklist expects at least one backup destination not continuously addressable by the operating system (offline) and full-system images of critical systems.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks backup plans, encryption with customer-managed keys, cross-region or cross-account copies and immutability (object lock or vault lock) for databases and object stores holding policyholder data; runtime-probe-prod-env and runtime-probe-datapipeline read backup job status. Evidence restore test reports per critical application (checklist Q243, Q244, Q247). Interval by category: the policy body says at a minimum every six months; Annexure II Q247 (RS.RP) and Q295 (WFRL) both read "Bi-annually, Bi-annually, Annual" for Cat-1, Cat-2 and Cat-3, where bi-annually means twice a year. Insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries: a restore test older than 6 months is a finding (param restoreTestIntervalMonths); Cat-3 intermediaries: older than 12 months (param restoreTestIntervalMonthsCat3). Annexure II Q243 also limits the offline backup destination for Cat-3 to sensitive data. Insurers are audited against the Guidelines body and the Annexure III checklist, which has no category columns, so they take the strictest (Cat-1) value. Intermediaries take the column for their Annexure II gross-insurance-revenue category (Cat-1 >= Rs 50 crore or any ISNP or web aggregator, Cat-2 Rs 5 to 50 crore, Cat-3 < Rs 5 crore); there is no reCategory slug for this yet (see 1.4-a), so read the category from details.json regulatoryRegistrations or the latest Annexure III report and apply it manually.
evidenceExpected: Backup and restoration standard by data classification
Backup encryption and immutable or offline copy configuration
Restore test reports within the category interval (6 months, or 12 months for Cat-3 intermediaries) for each critical system
Backup job monitoring and failure tickets

params.label: Maximum interval between data restoration tests (insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries)
Maximum interval between data restoration tests for Cat-3 intermediaries (Annexure II Q247, Q295: Annual)

controls.title: Patch management with defined timelines, classification and testing
controls.prose: The team maintaining information systems shall keep an inventory of software components, monitor vendor announcements for security patches and take each patch through evaluation of relevance and whether it is a normal or emergency change. A process shall define the number of days within which identified patches are applied and parameters for classifying patches; patches shall be tested in the organisation's test environment, business-critical applications tested before operating system or database patches, and hot-fix or critical patches directed by the regulator, advisories or OEMs may be fast-tracked with CISO and CTO approval. Endpoint patches shall be deployed within reasonable time of a device joining the network.
controls.guidance: Use sdlc/policy.json vulnerabilitySlaDays as the documented patch timeline and check it exists for every severity. runtime-probe-appcontainers and runtime-probe-prod-env list OS packages, base images and Kubernetes versions; cve-enrichment marks CISA KEV and CERT-In advisory CVEs and computes age past the policy days. Evidence patch test records and CISO/CTO approvals for emergency patches (checklist Q205, Q207, Q209 to Q211, Q213).
evidenceExpected: Patch management policy with patch classification and days-to-patch by severity
Patch compliance reports for servers, containers and endpoints
Test environment patch validation records
CISO and CTO approvals for emergency patches

controls.title: Capacity and performance monitoring with a capacity plan
controls.prose: Controls shall monitor the utilisation and performance of information systems so availability requirements are met at all times. Monitoring results should be analysed for security incidents and for trends that require changes or augmentation; a capacity management plan shall account for normal workloads, special contingencies and storage, thresholds shall be documented and monitored, future capacity projected, and system tuning applied. Service levels shall be defined per system with breaches affecting security raised as incidents.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env reads autoscaling, resource limits and alerting rules for critical services; probe-app-chart checks resource requests, limits and HPA definitions. Evidence capacity plan and threshold alerts routed to on-call (alerting.pagerdutyServiceIds in env files) (checklist Q3).
evidenceExpected: Capacity management plan with projections
Utilisation dashboards and threshold alert definitions
Service level definitions and breach reports

controls.title: Real-time malware protection on all endpoints, servers and gateways
controls.prose: Documented procedures shall cover prevention, detection and recovery from malicious code. All servers, desktops, workstations, hand-held devices, gateways and access points shall have real-time protection against viruses, trojans, malware, adware and spyware, updated periodically from an authentic source; unauthorised software execution shall be prevented, detections reported to a monitored enterprise system with unresolved malware raised as incidents, critical systems reviewed for unapproved files or changes, business continuity plans cover recovery from malware, and new malware intelligence collected regularly. Host, network or application IDS, hardened kernels and anti-ransomware controls are expected by the audit checklist.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env verifies EDR or runtime security agent (for example Falco or a cloud workload protection agent) coverage on nodes and that detections reach the SIEM; runtime-probe-harnesses and runtime-probe-sandboxes check the same for agent and code-execution sandboxes. Evidence EDR console coverage report versus asset inventory and file integrity monitoring on critical files (checklist Q214).
evidenceExpected: EDR or anti-malware coverage report against the asset inventory
Signature or engine update status
Malware detection alerts forwarded to SIEM and incident tickets
File integrity monitoring on critical systems

controls.title: Vulnerability management tracking CERT-In, NCIIPC and IRDAI advisories, with red team exercises
controls.prose: Technical vulnerabilities of systems and network equipment shall be identified periodically through scanning, with defined roles for monitoring, risk assessment, patching and coordination. The IS Operations team shall keep track of vendor security lists, anti-virus alerts and advisories from CERT, NCIIPC and IRDAI, the organisation should track the mapping of notifications and advisories from CERT-In, NCCC, NCIIPC and IRDAI to its estate, a timeline shall be defined to react to them, and the team shall assess the real risk of each vulnerability and mitigate it, including client-side vulnerabilities. Periodic red team exercises shall test readiness to detect and respond, with results documented in open machine-readable formats such as SCAP and scored for comparison over time. An audit log shall be kept, the process monitored for effectiveness and aligned with incident management, and a channel provided for external parties to report vulnerabilities.
controls.guidance: Maxwell's cves/ store and cve-enrichment provide the advisory mapping: every open soc finding with a CVE should carry advisory references and a slaDueAt from the sla-table. Evidence authenticated scan coverage, the advisory tracker including CERT-In advisories, a security.txt or responsible disclosure page (runtime-probe-network-perimeter) and the latest red team report with score trend (checklist Q39, Q59, Q83, Q223, Q239).
evidenceExpected: Vulnerability scanning schedule and coverage reports
Advisory tracker mapping CERT-In, NCIIPC and IRDAI advisories to assets
Red team exercise reports with scoring
Vulnerability disclosure channel

controls.title: Separate development, test and production environments
controls.prose: Development, testing and operational environments should be separated to reduce the risk of unauthorised access or changes to production, with documented rules for promoting software to production. Development and operational software shall run on different systems or domains, changes shall be tested in a test or staging environment first, compilers, editors and development utilities shall not be accessible from operational systems when not required, sensitive data shall not be copied to test unless equivalent controls apply, and users shall have different profiles for operational and test systems. Developers should not have unmonitored access to production.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks that production runs in separate cloud accounts or subscriptions and VPCs from dev and QA; runtime-probe-devtest-env and runtime-probe-qa-env verify no network path or shared credentials to production data stores; runtime-probe-appcontainers flags shells, compilers and package managers in production images; runtime-probe-identity-access flags developer principals with standing production write access (checklist Q51).
evidenceExpected: Account, subscription or cluster separation for production and non-production
Promotion rules documented in the release process
Network policy and IAM evidence blocking non-production access to production data
Production images without development tooling

controls.title: Controlled installation of operational software with rollback and version retention
controls.prose: Procedures shall control installation of software on operational systems; operational software, applications and program libraries shall be updated only by trained administrators with management authorisation, all implemented software and documentation kept under a configuration control system, a rollback strategy in place before changes, an audit log of updates to operational libraries maintained, and previous versions retained as contingency and archived with parameters and configuration for as long as related data is retained. Scheduled production jobs shall be inventoried with interdependencies, approved by system owners, monitored, reviewed and failures raised as incidents.
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env verifies deployments to production happen only through the pipeline with signed and versioned artefacts retained in the registry, and that rollback is documented per sdlc/policy.json rollbackPlanRequired; runtime-probe-prod-env checks for workloads not deployed by the pipeline (manual kubectl or console changes) and for batch or cron jobs without monitoring. Evidence the job schedule inventory for core policy and claims batch runs.
evidenceExpected: Deployment audit log showing pipeline-only production changes
Artefact registry retention of previous versions
Rollback procedure per application
Production job schedule inventory with monitoring

controls.title: Registered mobile devices under centralised MDM with remote wipe and encryption
controls.prose: Access to business information from mobile devices shall follow a signed end-user agreement accepting duties, waiving ownership of business data and permitting remote wipe on loss, theft or withdrawal of authorisation, with separation of private and business use. All mobile devices shall be registered and authenticated before connecting, managed through a centralised MDM solution that at minimum supports remote wipe and hardware or file-based encryption, access granted per business need, lost devices or media reported immediately for wiping, MDM logs recorded and users trained on mobile risks.
controls.guidance: Evidence MDM enrolment coverage against devices accessing email and sales or claims apps, compliance policies (encryption, passcode, OS version) and conditional access blocking unenrolled devices, checked by runtime-probe-identity-access on the IdP. Evidence wipe logs for reported losses.
evidenceExpected: MDM enrolment and compliance report
Signed end-user agreements for mobile access
Conditional access policy blocking unmanaged devices
Remote wipe logs

controls.title: Minimum security configuration on BYOD smartphones and tablets
controls.prose: Personally owned smartphones and tablets may access corporate email, applications and data only under the BYOD programme: IT maintains a whitelist of supported models and OS versions, rooted or jailbroken and unlicensed OS devices are not supported, and devices are enrolled through a self-service portal with MDM controls. Minimum controls are a 4-digit passcode or pattern, automatic wipe of corporate data after 10 unsuccessful attempts, two-factor authentication for corporate applications and data, device lock after 5 minutes of inactivity, device tracking, remote lock and erase, jailbreak detection, data encryption and containerisation, and application blacklisting. Loss of a device shall be reported to IT within 4 hours for remote wipe, absconding employees' devices wiped on HR notice, and a failed wipe reported as a security incident.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access reads the MDM or app-protection policy (Intune, Workspace ONE or similar) for passcode, wipe-after-failures, inactivity lock, jailbreak detection and containerisation settings and compares them to the parameters. Weaker settings are findings unless an approved exception exists.
evidenceExpected: BYOD policy and signed user acceptance
MDM or app-protection policy settings export
Supported device and OS whitelist
Device loss reports and wipe records

params.label: Unsuccessful logon attempts after which corporate data is wiped
Inactivity before device lock
Hours within which device loss must be reported to IT

controls.title: Formal change lifecycle with TRA, approval, testing, rollback and emergency change controls
controls.prose: All changes to information resources shall follow a documented change management procedure. Changes shall be classified by data impacted and impact on the IT environment; major and identified change types go through a technology risk assessment reviewed by the IS team. The lifecycle requires a recorded request with business requirement and impact analysis (financial, operational, regulatory, technology), approval per the change authorisation matrix, prioritisation, testing in the test environment (SAT, SIT, UAT as applicable), migration to production only by authorised individuals, and documentation updates with test records retained; all changes should include a rollback procedure for aborting and recovering from failed changes. Development and test environments shall be segregated from production with no user accessing both simultaneously, and production data preferably not moved to test unless protected equally. Website updates shall be independently reviewed, approved and tested. Emergency changes may bypass the lifecycle but shall be documented with post-facto approval and an audit log, and verbal approvals confirmed by email from the Head of Operations. Releases follow a formal release process with version control, advance communication and a release document.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc and probe-cicd-env compare sdlc/policy.json (codeReview.required, minApprovers, selfApprovalAllowed false, approvalsRequired for production, rollbackPlanRequired, emergencyChangeProcess) with actual repository and pipeline settings, and sample production deployments for linked change tickets and approvals. impl-change-management records IRDAI-relevant changes in change_management/master.json with TRA references. Direct pushes or unreviewed merges to production branches are findings (checklist Q191, Q265).
evidenceExpected: Change management procedure and authorisation matrix
Sample change records with impact analysis, TRA, approvals, test evidence and rollback plan
Emergency change log with post-facto approvals
Branch protection and deployment approval settings
Release documents with version control

controls.title: Incident response organisation, reporting mechanisms and classification
controls.prose: The organisation shall implement procedures for detecting, reporting, responding to, analysing and tracking incidents to closure. An Incident Response Team shall operate with the CRO and COO as Incident Management Leader (the only role that may speak to the media), the CISO and CTO as Incident Management Coordinator, and team leaders for business continuity, IT, information security (the CISO) and physical incidents, with emergency contacts of the team, vendors and service providers available. All users, contractors and third parties shall have mechanisms to report incidents and weaknesses in reasonable time, and monitoring shall detect malfunctions. Every incident shall be recorded with source, impacted assets, description and times of occurrence, detection and recording; classified High, Medium or Low by impact, scope and data classification; categorised as IS, IT or non-IT; responded to by a nominated point of contact; and subject to post-incident analysis. All incidents shall be reported to the CISO and response activities logged, with resolution within IS-team timelines per classification and escalation of those open beyond SLA to the CRO and ISRMC.
controls.guidance: Maxwell's soc incident records are the register: each needs severity, detectedAt, acknowledgedAt, containedAt, affectedAssets, affectedDataClassifications and a timeline; refresh-soc flags incidents without classification or past their resolution SLA. Evidence the incident response plan naming IML, IMC and team leaders, the reporting channels (helpdesk, email, portal) and PagerDuty or ticketing exports (checklist Q85, Q227, Q238, Q251, Q254).
evidenceExpected: Incident response plan with IRT roles (IML, IMC, team leaders) and emergency contact list
Incident register with classification, category and timestamps
Post-incident analysis reports
Escalations of incidents breaching resolution SLA to CRO and ISRMC

controls.title: 24x7 SOC monitoring through SIEM with detective controls on critical systems
controls.prose: Enterprise-wide monitoring of information security incidents shall be performed by the SOC on a 24x7 basis, with continuous monitoring of IT logs for unauthorised logins and logouts, access violations and similar events through a Security Information and Event Management system. The CISO should ensure logging and monitoring on all critical infrastructure systems and detective controls such as file integrity monitoring or hashing on critical files and systems. Appropriate contacts with relevant authorities shall be maintained for escalation.
controls.guidance: For each production environment in applications/<app_id>/env/<env_id>.json, observability.siem must be set; runtime-probe-prod-env verifies cloud audit logs, Kubernetes audit logs, WAF, database and IdP logs are forwarded, and that detection rules exist for anomalous login behaviour (time, location) and access to deactivated accounts. Evidence SOC shift rosters, SIEM use-case list and tuning records (checklist Q2, Q5, Q24, Q35, Q55, Q56).
evidenceExpected: SIEM log source coverage for critical systems
SOC 24x7 roster or managed SOC SLA
Detection use-case catalogue including anomalous login behaviour
File integrity monitoring configuration on critical systems

controls.title: Notification to regulatory authorities: reporting routes, timelines and 6-hour CERT-In report
controls.prose: The organisation shall identify how incidents shall be reported to internal parties and external organisations (e.g. regulators, media, law enforcement, customers, IRDAI, CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin, Cyber Swachhta Kendra), and the timelines prescribed for reporting incidents to external organisations shall be strictly adhered to. It shall mandatorily report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing or being brought to notice about such incidents, with a copy to IRDAI and other concerned regulators or authorities, using the methods and formats published on the CERT-In website. It shall ensure that contact details of ministries, stakeholders, vendors and agencies such as NCIIPC and CERT-In for incident resolution are up to date and documented.
controls.guidance: This is the whole of policy 2.10 para 3.5 (items 1 to 4); the 6-hour clock alone is also catalogued as 2.10-3.5.3 for precise citation. The instruments registry hardRequirements and the sla-table incident-reporting row cite this id. Evidence the incident communication matrix (internal escalation, IRDAI, CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin, law enforcement, customers), a contact list reviewed in the last year, and for every reportable soc incident two regulatorReportRefs (CERT-In with deadlineHours 6 and the IRDAI copy with deadlineHours 6 from detectedAt). The CISO is responsible for reporting critical or high severity incidents to regulators (1.6-3); the IRDAI 24-hour detailed format is CIR-128.3. No slaDays: 6 hours is a reporting window taken from the sla-table incident-reporting row and param certInReportingHours, not a remediation period; a finding about a missing or weak procedure takes its deadline from the SLA table by severity. Checklist Q229, Q231, Q232.
evidenceExpected: Incident communication matrix naming internal parties, IRDAI, CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin and law enforcement
CERT-In submission acknowledgements with timestamps within 6 hours of detection
Copy of each CERT-In report sent to IRDAI
Current contact list for CERT-In, NCIIPC, IRDAI, ministries and key vendors

params.label: Hours from noticing a cyber incident within which CERT-In must be informed, with a copy to IRDAI

controls.title: Report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours with a copy to IRDAI
controls.prose: Organisation shall mandatorily report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing or being brought to notice about such incidents, with a copy to IRDAI and other concerned regulators or authorities. The details regarding methods and formats of reporting cyber incidents are published on the CERT-In website.
controls.guidance: Item 3 of policy 2.10 para 3.5; the parent 2.10-3.5 carries the full clause (reporting routes, adherence to timelines, contact list) and is the id the registry and sla-table cite. Each soc incident meeting the CERT-In Annexure I categories must carry two regulatorReportRefs: CERT-In with deadlineHours 6 and IRDAI (copy) with deadlineHours 6 from detectedAt, each with submittedAt and reference; refresh-soc raises a finding when either is missing or late. The IRDAI 24-hour detailed format under circular 128 is a separate control (CIR-128.3). No slaDays: 6 hours is a reporting window (param certInReportingHours, sla-table incident-reporting row for 2.10-3.5), not a remediation period for a gap. Checklist Q229, Q231, Q232.
evidenceExpected: CERT-In submission acknowledgements with timestamps within 6 hours of detection
Copy of each CERT-In report sent to IRDAI

params.label: Hours from noticing a cyber incident within which CERT-In must be informed, with a copy to IRDAI

controls.title: Root cause analysis, problem management and incident knowledge base
controls.prose: Incident records shall be analysed periodically to identify trends and diagnose root and contributing causes so preventive measures reduce recurrence; problems shall be assigned for resolution within timelines based on the criticality of source incidents and fixes implemented through change management. Internal procedures shall govern handling of evidence for disciplinary and legal action. Resolutions and known causes shall be recorded in a knowledge base accessible to incident teams, and lessons from incident evaluation used to identify recurring or high-impact incidents and quantify their types, impacts and costs. Root cause analysis and action taken reports shall be provided to the concerned insurer on demand.
controls.guidance: refresh-soc checks that closed high-severity incidents carry rootCause and a postmortemUrl, and that corrective actions link to initiatives in change_management/master.json. Evidence the quarterly incident trend review and forensic evidence handling procedure (checklist Q221, Q226, Q233, Q237, Q252).
evidenceExpected: RCA reports for high and medium severity incidents
Problem records linked to change requests
Incident trend analysis presented to ISRMC
Evidence handling (chain of custody) procedure

controls.title: Controlled connectivity, MFA for remote access to transaction systems and dedicated admin workstations
controls.prose: Networks shall be secured against unauthorised access and used only for business purposes with formally approved access.
