Responsibilities for network equipment management shall be established, special controls protect data over public and wireless networks, logging and monitoring record relevant actions, systems on the network should be authenticated and their connection to the network shall be restricted, and the security of network service providers determined, monitored and subject to a right to audit. External connectivity to the internal network is permitted only through authorised MPLS, point-to-point links or VPN, every connection is protected by perimeter devices, all entry points reviewed and approved, and connections to business transaction and high-severity systems from outside organisation-controlled networks require two-factor authentication with device compliance checks. Network engineers shall use a dedicated, segmented administrative machine without internet access, only authorised scripting languages and fully supported browsers and email clients shall run, and personal communications equipment attached to PCs is prohibited.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter enumerates internet-exposed endpoints from DNS and cloud load balancers and checks that admin interfaces (Kubernetes API, databases, SSH, RDP) are not publicly reachable; probe-iac checks security groups and firewall rules for 0.0.0.0/0 on management ports and that bastion or privileged access workstation patterns are used. runtime-probe-identity-access confirms MFA and device posture on VPN or ZTNA (checklist Q32, Q52, Q53).
evidenceExpected: Approved list of network entry points and connectivity modes
Firewall and security group rules for management interfaces
VPN or ZTNA MFA and device compliance configuration
Privileged access workstation or bastion design

controls.title: Segment networks by data classification and isolate monetary transaction systems
controls.prose: The network shall be segmented according to the label or classification of information on the servers, with all sensitive information located on separated VLANs, adequate measures taken to isolate and secure the perimeter and connectivity of servers running monetary transaction applications and processes, and preventive controls blocking unauthorised collaboration tools at firewalls or network security devices. The audit checklist also expects workstation-to-workstation communication disabled (private VLANs or micro-segmentation) and separate networks for untrusted devices.
controls.guidance: probe-iac and probe-app-chart check that payment, premium collection and claims payout services sit in dedicated subnets or namespaces with default-deny Kubernetes NetworkPolicies and security groups; runtime-probe-prod-env tests east-west reachability from a non-sensitive namespace to databases holding confidential data (read-only connection attempts per rules of engagement). Flat networks are high findings (checklist Q25, Q66, Q212).
evidenceExpected: Network segmentation design mapped to data classification
Default-deny network policies for sensitive workloads
Isolation evidence for monetary transaction systems
Firewall rules blocking unauthorised collaboration tools

controls.title: Perimeter device inventory, MBSS compliance and application whitelisting
controls.prose: Perimeter security systems such as firewalls and IDS shall be deployed with procedures to protect all information assets at network level, and an inventory of all perimeter devices maintained and updated periodically and on every network change. MBSS shall be defined for every make, model and version of perimeter device, changed only through change management and reviewed periodically, with mechanisms detecting and addressing deviations of actual configurations from the baseline or approving them as exceptions. Application whitelisting software shall ensure only authorised software libraries load into processes and only authorised, digitally signed scripts run. Network equipment, communication lines and LAN/WAN network diagrams shall be documented and kept current, and an active discovery tool shall identify sensitive information across on-site and service-provider systems to update the sensitive information inventory.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks cloud firewall, WAF and IDS resources are declared in code with drift detection; runtime-probe-network-perimeter compares device and cloud firewall configurations against baseline rules. For workloads, probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers check image signature verification and admission policies as the container equivalent of whitelisting; runtime-probe-harnesses checks agent harness tool and script allow-lists. Evidence network diagrams dated within the review period (checklist Q115, Q193, Q196, Q197, Q242, Q246).
evidenceExpected: Perimeter device inventory
MBSS per perimeter device type and configuration compliance reports
Current network architecture diagrams
Application whitelisting or image signature enforcement policies
Sensitive data discovery tool reports

controls.title: Proxy-controlled egress, WAF for web applications and URL categorisation
controls.prose: Traffic to public networks such as the internet shall pass through gateway systems such as proxy servers in addition to perimeter security, access to external resources shall follow business need and access control procedures, connecting organisation mobile assets to unauthorised Wi-Fi hotspots is prohibited, and third parties providing network services shall be bound to the network policy. Web applications shall be protected by web application firewalls inspecting all traffic for common attacks, with application firewalls for non-web applications where available; if traffic is encrypted the device shall sit behind the encryption or decrypt it, otherwise a host-based WAF shall be deployed. URL categorisation services shall be subscribed to and uncategorised sites blocked by default.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter verifies each internet-facing application (customer portal, agent portal, partner APIs, web aggregator integrations) is fronted by a WAF in blocking mode with OWASP managed rules and that TLS terminates before inspection; probe-iac checks WAF association on load balancers and API gateways and that workload egress goes through a controlled NAT or proxy with allow-lists. runtime-probe-harnesses checks governed egress for AI agent runtimes (checklist Q31, Q47, Q60, Q62, Q67).
evidenceExpected: WAF association and rule configuration per internet-facing application
Egress proxy or NAT allow-list configuration
URL categorisation policy blocking uncategorised sites
Web access logs

controls.title: Encrypt information by classification in transit, on media and at rest
controls.prose: Cryptographic controls shall be applied according to the encryption requirements of the data classification policy, based on a risk assessment of need, methodology and business areas. Confidential and Restricted information shall be encrypted when transported on mobile or removable media or across communication lines; critical information not actively used shall be encrypted when stored or transported on computer-readable media such as servers, tapes, laptop disks and mobile memory wherever feasible; and static or reusable authentication information shall be encrypted in storage and in transit. The audit checklist expects standardised, extensively reviewed algorithms, AES for wireless, full-disk encryption on mobile devices and encryption of all sensitive information in transit.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks encryption at rest with customer-managed keys on databases, object storage, volumes and backups, and TLS 1.2+ enforcement on load balancers; runtime-probe-network-perimeter tests TLS versions and cipher suites on public endpoints; probe-schemas and execute-scr look for plaintext storage of passwords, card, bank or health data and weak hashing. Deprecated protocols or unencrypted confidential stores are high findings (checklist Q29, Q30, Q46, Q77, Q81).
evidenceExpected: Encryption standard mapped to data classification
At-rest encryption configuration for data stores and backups
TLS configuration scan of external and internal endpoints
Password hashing and credential storage review

controls.title: Cryptographic key management across the full key lifecycle
controls.prose: A policy on the use, protection and lifetime of cryptographic keys shall be implemented through their whole lifecycle, including recovery of encrypted information when keys are lost, compromised or damaged. Keys shall be protected against modification and loss, algorithm type and strength chosen by criticality and key lengths complying with contractual and regulatory requirements, keys not transmitted over the network unless over secure channels, and activation and deactivation dates defined. The lifecycle covers creation in a hardened environment with separation of duties, backup to protected storage, tested deployment, monitoring for unauthorised key management operations, expiration aligned with data validity and secure destruction, with key management activities logged and audited.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks KMS or HSM keys for rotation enabled, key policies limiting administrators separately from users, deletion protection and CloudTrail or equivalent logging of key operations; probe-cicd-env and probe-sdlc check that no private keys or certificates are committed to repositories or baked into images (secret scanning results). Evidence the key inventory with owners and rotation dates.
evidenceExpected: Key management policy and key inventory with owners and validity
KMS or HSM rotation and access policy configuration
Audit logs of key management operations
Secret scanning results for repositories and images

params.label: Maximum key validity before rotation, as set in the organisation's key management policy (the Guidelines state no number)

groups.title: 2.13 Business Continuity Management and Disaster Recovery

controls.title: Business impact analysis with RTO and RPO for every application
controls.prose: A single BCM framework shall hold documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans covering enterprise-wide continuation, critical applications, data centre DR, network links and roles. RTO and RPO shall be defined for all applications from business requirements, all business dependencies on IT systems documented, and every new application introduced shall have a documented IT DR process based on criticality integrated with existing recovery processes and a business-defined RTO and RPO. Threats that could disrupt IT assets shall be identified, a risk analysis performed at least annually against documented acceptable risk levels, and risk mitigation plans with owners approved by management and tracked to closure quarterly.
controls.guidance: Compare details.json criticalFunctions[].impactTolerance (maxOutageMinutes, maxDataLossMinutes) and appIds with each application's DR design; probe-iac checks multi-AZ or multi-region deployment and replication settings match the stated RPO. An application in applications/ without an RTO/RPO or with replication lag exceeding RPO is a finding (checklist Q248, Q250).
evidenceExpected: Business impact analysis with RTO and RPO per application
IT dependency map for critical business functions
Annual BCM risk analysis and quarterly mitigation plan tracking
DR design matching RTO and RPO for new applications

controls.title: IT DR plans with DC-DR parity, RPO-compliant replication and annual review
controls.prose: IT DR plans approved by the ISRMC shall be documented for each application with prioritised recovery objectives, invocation triggers, escalation stages and detailed restoration procedures for applications, databases, hardware, network access, data synchronisation and backlog handling. The DR environment shall be kept in sync with production at all times with all production changes applied to DR, server and network configurations at DC and DR identical, periodic data and transaction integrity checks between DC and DR, no single point of failure in supporting infrastructure, continuous operation data mirroring to the offsite location for inter-related applications, and replication ensuring RPO compliance for critical applications. Changes affecting recovery procedures shall be approved by the ITDR manager. IT DR plans shall be reviewed at least annually. Outsourced applications shall have continuity plans developed and tested by the provider and approved by the organisation.
controls.guidance: probe-iac compares primary and DR infrastructure code (same modules and versions per region), checks database replication configuration and that DR is part of the deployment pipeline so changes reach both sites; runtime-probe-prod-env reads replication lag and DR cluster versions. refresh-vendor-ctx collects provider DR test reports for outsourced core systems (checklist Q130, Q195).
evidenceExpected: Per-application IT DR plans approved by the ISRMC
DC and DR configuration parity reports
Replication lag monitoring against RPO
Annual DR plan review records
Service provider DR plans and test reports

controls.title: Test BCP and DR plans with realistic drills reported to ISRMC, at the checklist interval for the category
controls.prose: Business continuity and DR plans shall be tested at least once a year or when significantly changed to identify incorrect assumptions, oversights and changes in equipment or personnel. Test results shall be reported to the ISRMC and used to revise the plans, DR drills shall represent real disaster scenarios and not only planned shutdowns, tests shall be planned to avoid business disruption with risks communicated beforehand, alternative sites and resources tested, and staff with recovery roles trained. BCP shall be reviewed at its defined periodicity and after each test. The audit checklist additionally asks whether response plans are tested quarterly including recovery from backups, and whether the cyber crisis plan is rehearsed periodically.
controls.guidance: Collect the last DR drill report per critical application with actual recovery time and data loss against RTO and RPO, the ISRMC minutes where results were tabled, and remediation tasks created in change_management. Interval by category: the policy body sets at least once a year, but the Annexure II checklist is stricter for larger entities. Q329 (DR drills at the remote backup site, printed in the WFRL-Investment area and applied by auditors to DR drills generally) reads "Bi-annually, Bi-annually, Annual": insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries without a drill in the last 6 months have a high finding (param drDrillIntervalMonths), Cat-3 intermediaries only after 12 months (param drDrillIntervalMonthsCat3). Q241 (response plans tested including management and recovery from backups) reads "Yes, Annual, Annual" against a quarterly question: insurers and Cat-1 intermediaries test quarterly (param responsePlanTestIntervalMonths), Cat-2 and Cat-3 intermediaries annually (param responsePlanTestIntervalMonthsCat2Cat3); record a missed response-plan test as its own observation and finding. Insurers are audited against the Guidelines body and the Annexure III checklist, which has no category columns, so they take the strictest (Cat-1) value. Intermediaries take the column for their Annexure II gross-insurance-revenue category (Cat-1 >= Rs 50 crore or any ISNP or web aggregator, Cat-2 Rs 5 to 50 crore, Cat-3 < Rs 5 crore); there is no reCategory slug for this yet (see 1.4-a), so read the category from details.json regulatoryRegistrations or the latest Annexure III report and apply it manually.
evidenceExpected: DR drill reports with achieved RTO and RPO within the category interval
ISRMC minutes reviewing test results
Plan revisions following tests
Response plan and backup recovery test records (quarterly for insurers and Cat-1 intermediaries)

params.label: Maximum interval between DR drills for insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries (Annexure II Q329: Bi-annually; body minimum annual)
Maximum interval between DR drills for Cat-3 intermediaries (Annexure II Q329: Annual)
Maximum interval between response plan tests including recovery from backups for insurers and Cat-1 intermediaries (Q241: quarterly)
Maximum interval between response plan tests for Cat-2 and Cat-3 intermediaries (Annexure II Q241: Annual)

controls.title: Security obligations, NDA and right to audit in every third-party contract
controls.prose: All contracts with third-party service providers shall require controls complying with the organisation's information security policy for the assets they access, at a level at least as secure as the organisation provides internally. A non-disclosure agreement shall be signed where confidential information is involved, compliance assessment shall be included in the agreement, no information exchange shall occur and no access be granted before a signed written agreement. Contracts shall be drafted by Legal with Compliance, Risk and IS, define security requirements by vendor classification, carry SLAs monitored at the defined periodicity and build in the right to audit. A vendor certified to ISO 27001 with the services in scope may be exempted from periodic audits if it furnishes a self-certificate of compliance with the contract's IS provisions and a copy of the valid certificate.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx populates vendors/<vendor_id>.json contract (rightToAudit, dataReturnAndDeletion, subcontractingAllowed, exitPlanDocumented) and assurance (ISO 27001 certificate with scope and expiresAt, self-certificate). Findings: critical vendor without rightToAudit, expired certificate, ISO scope not covering the service, or access in place without a signed contract (checklist Q141 to Q143, Q230).
evidenceExpected: Signed contracts with IS clauses, NDA and right to audit
SLA monitoring reports
ISO 27001 certificate with scope covering the service and vendor self-certificate
Evidence that access was granted only after contract signature

controls.title: Vendor classification, due diligence and periodic assessment
controls.prose: All third-party service providers shall be classified under an IS-team standard considering the nature of the activity, classification of information accessed, access to premises, operational criticality, access to intellectual property, regulatory significance of the service and availability of alternative providers; the standard defines security requirements, assessment periodicity and mechanism, and contractual requirements such as escrow or SLAs per class. The business shall perform due diligence before enrolment or on change of services, by vendor self-appraisal, on-site visit or public information, covering experience and competence, reputation, compliance and litigation, security policies and controls, audit coverage and BCM, the political, economic and legal environment of the vendor's jurisdiction, employee due diligence and sub-contracting arrangements. Every provider shall be periodically assessed for SLA performance, competent personnel not barred by regulators, adequate infrastructure and documentation, conflicts of interest and compliance with IS and confidentiality provisions. Third-party access to sensitive information shall be monitored.
controls.guidance: vendor-analyst sets materiality, substitutability and criticality per service in vendors/<vendor_id>.json and records lastAssessment with date, rating and assessor; refresh-vendor-ctx flags critical vendors (TPAs, cloud providers, core policy administration and claims platforms, call centres) whose last assessment is older than the periodicity in the classification standard, and subcontractors not assessed. Store the classification standard periodicity in the soc control record parameter.
evidenceExpected: Vendor classification standard with assessment periodicity by class
Due diligence reports at onboarding including sub-contractors
Periodic vendor assessment reports
Monitoring of third-party access to sensitive information

params.label: Assessment periodicity for the highest vendor class, as defined in the organisation's classification standard (the Guidelines state no number)

controls.title: Third-party termination, data handover, deletion and no onward sharing
controls.prose: The organisation reserves the right to terminate a provider for non-performance or non-conformity with contractual requirements, with termination clauses in the contract. On termination or expiry the provider shall return organisation assets and access to information assets and premises shall be revoked immediately or on the expiry date. Data shared must have a valid business purpose; data generated by the third party for the organisation belongs to the organisation and follows its policies; data held by or in transit with the third party is subject to the same or stricter controls by classification; the organisation may delete its data from vendor assets with certification; all data transferred or generated shall be handed over on termination; and the third party shall not share data with any other entity without explicit approval and a contract mandating compliance.
controls.guidance: For vendors with status ending or terminated in vendors/<vendor_id>.json, runtime-probe-identity-access checks for remaining vendor accounts, API keys, VPN profiles and cross-account IAM roles; refresh-vendor-ctx collects the data return and deletion certificate. Evidence purpose documentation for data shared with each vendor and approvals for onward sharing to sub-processors.
evidenceExpected: Termination clauses and exit plans in contracts
Access revocation evidence on contract end
Data handover and deletion certificates
Approvals for onward data sharing by vendors

controls.title: Security zones with restricted, reviewed access to server rooms and data centres
controls.prose: Facilities shall be divided into zones: Zone 1 semi-public areas protected by guards, Zone 2 work areas controlled by access cards, Zone 3 secured areas with confidential data or valuables such as dealing rooms, and Zone 4 electronically sensitive areas such as server rooms, data centres and hub rooms. Zones 3 and 4 shall be located away from entry and exit points without explicit signage, have a designated owner who identifies authorised persons, validates the list periodically and revokes unnecessary access, and be accessed only on absolute need through automated access control (or lock and key or guards), with long-term access reviewed half-yearly and service providers and visitors escorted with explicit owner approval. Visitors are recorded and escorted, badges are personal and non-transferable, and breaches are reported to the site in-charge and CISO. The audit checklist expects CCTV, card access, mantraps and immediate revocation of physical access no longer required.
controls.guidance: For cloud-hosted estates, collect the cloud provider's SOC 2 or ISO 27001 physical control attestations through refresh-vendor-ctx (vendors assurance) and confine direct evidence to offices, on-premises server rooms and any co-location racks. Evidence half-yearly access reviews of Zone 3 and Zone 4 lists and visitor logs (checklist Q153, Q158, Q159).
evidenceExpected: Zone classification of premises with zone owners
Half-yearly access reviews for Zone 3 and Zone 4
Access control system and CCTV logs
Visitor registers with escort records
Cloud or co-location provider physical security attestations

params.label: Review interval for access rights to Zone 3 and Zone 4 sensitive areas

controls.title: Environmental protection for data centres and server rooms
controls.prose: Environmental controls shall protect people and infrastructure from fire, flood, power failure, temperature extremes and earthquakes, designed by administration and overseen by the CISO. Buildings shall have minimal entry points, unlocked fire exits with alarms, tested lightning protection and backup power (DG sets and UPS for critical resources), with a technical team monitoring environmental parameters. Work areas shall have water intrusion and temperature monitoring, fire exits, extinguishers, smoke detectors, displayed floor plans and evacuation drills at least annually. Sensitive areas shall have water leakage monitoring by BMS, smoke detection, intrusion alarms (physical intrusions treated as security breaches), automated fire detection and suppression, fire-resistant construction, frequent temperature monitoring, precision air conditioning and dual power supply. Assets moving out of Zones 3 and 4 require authorisation and secure transport.
controls.guidance: Evidence BMS monitoring reports, fire suppression maintenance certificates, UPS and DG test logs and the annual evacuation drill record for owned facilities; for cloud regions rely on provider attestations. Maxwell records these as manual-method observations since no probe reaches physical plant (checklist Q109, Q110).
evidenceExpected: BMS environmental monitoring reports for server rooms
Fire detection and suppression maintenance certificates
UPS, DG and dual power test records
Annual evacuation drill record

controls.title: Log all system, privileged and application activity, protect logs and make them available to authorities
controls.prose: All critical systems shall be monitored through real-time alerting, logging of all activities and transactions with periodic analysis, and periodic security posture assessments. Logging shall be enabled for all business transactions and high-risk systems with real-time or periodic review, systems configured to log activity and alert on unusual activity, privileged user and operator activity logged, protected and independently reviewed, policy violations detected, manual log review performed where automated alerts are absent, and actions on alerts routed through incident and change management. Application logs shall capture start and stop times, errors and corrective actions, handling of critical files and output, the person, process or system making the entry and the source IP or MAC address, and applications shall prevent the same user ID logging in from multiple workstations simultaneously. All communication with external networks shall be logged and reviewed. Logs shall be retained per record retention and regulatory requirements, protected against tampering and unauthorised access, and made available to law enforcement agencies, IRDAI, CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin when required.
controls.guidance: probe-app-chart and execute-scr check application logging includes user identity, source IP and outcome for authentication, policy issuance, endorsement, claims approval and payout events; probe-iac checks audit logging on cloud control planes, databases and storage with write-once or restricted-delete log buckets; runtime-probe-prod-env confirms logs arrive in the SIEM and that operators cannot delete them. Evidence privileged activity review sign-offs (checklist Q16, Q47, Q151, Q175).
evidenceExpected: Logging standard specifying required events and fields
Cloud, database, Kubernetes and application audit log configuration
Log integrity protection (immutability, restricted delete)
Independent reviews of privileged user logs
Procedure for providing logs to IRDAI, CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin and law enforcement

controls.title: Synchronise clocks to an agreed accurate reference time source
controls.prose: Clocks of all relevant information processing systems shall be synchronised with an agreed accurate time source, external and internal requirements for time representation, synchronisation and accuracy documented, and a standard reference time defined for the organisation. The audit checklist asks whether information assets are synchronised with a singular time source.
controls.guidance: Evaluate together with cert-in-directions-2022 Dir-i (NIC or NPL NTP or traceable sources): probe-iac and probe-app-chart check chrony or cloud time-service configuration in images and node pools, runtime-probe-prod-env measures drift. Evidence the documented reference time standard (checklist Q99).
evidenceExpected: Time synchronisation standard naming the reference source
NTP client configuration per environment
Clock drift measurements

controls.title: Retain ICT infrastructure logs for a rolling 180 days within India
controls.prose: ICT infrastructure logs shall be maintained as per regulatory guidelines, for a rolling period of 180 days and within the Indian jurisdiction, as per directions issued by CERT-In from time to time. The audit checklist asks auditors to verify both the 180-day retention and that ICT infrastructure, critical and business data are stored in India.
controls.guidance: For every environment in applications/<app_id>/env/<env_id>.json check observability.logsRetentionDays >= 180 and logsInIndia true; probe-iac verifies log bucket lifecycle rules, SIEM hot plus archive retention and that log storage regions are ap-south-1, ap-south-2, asia-south1, asia-south2, centralindia or another Indian region, and runtime-probe-prod-env confirms the SIEM or log vendor's storage location. A SaaS log platform storing outside India is a high finding (checklist Q145). The registry hardRequirements cite this log-retention obligation as policy "2.16". Annexure II Q146 asks whether "ICT infrastructure logs, Critical and Business data" are stored in India, so a log store outside India also fails that question (see Annex-III.146).
evidenceExpected: Log retention configuration showing at least 180 days
Log storage region evidence within India
SIEM or log vendor data residency documentation

params.label: Rolling retention period for ICT infrastructure logs within India

controls.title: Monitor user accounts for unwanted privileges, orphan and dormant accounts
controls.prose: User accounts shall be monitored regularly to detect unwanted privileges, orphan accounts and dormant accounts, with violating accounts suspended or terminated; redundant or dormant IDs shall not be reissued; and periodic account reviews shall require managers to match current rights with business requirements. The audit checklist expects dormant accounts to be disabled automatically after a set period of inactivity and all accounts to carry monitored expiration dates.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access reports accounts with no login beyond the dormancy threshold set in the soc control parameters, accounts without an owner or HR record, and accounts lacking expiry (contractors, vendors); these become findings unless suspended (checklist Q10, Q26, Q33).
evidenceExpected: Dormant and orphan account reports
Automated dormancy disablement configuration
Manager account review sign-offs

params.label: Inactivity period after which accounts are disabled, as set by the organisation (the Guidelines state no number)

controls.title: Security assessment standards and VAPT calendar by application criticality
controls.prose: The IS team shall define standards for vulnerability assessment and security review of infrastructure and applications covering the frequency of assessments by application criticality, coverage, and the internal versus external approach. Network and application vulnerability assessments shall be performed on an ongoing basis by competent personnel with risks documented in assessment reports, results analysed and acted on by system owners, all reports and actions reviewed by the IS team, unmitigated risks due to technology or business constraints escalated to the ISRMC for resolution or exception approval, and results communicated to relevant vendors. The audit checklist expects a defined VAPT procedure and calendar, a closure tracker, penetration test accounts that are controlled and removed after testing, and a pen-test programme covering blended wireless, client-side and web attacks.
controls.guidance: Store assessment frequency per application tier in the soc control record parameters and details.json vaptPerYear and lastVaptAt; refresh-soc checks each VAPT finding is imported with a fingerprint, severity and slaDueAt, and that risks left open beyond SLA have an ISRMC-approved soc risk acceptance (checklist Q6, Q40, Q79, Q89, Q90, Q92). The sla-table patch-sla and audit-cadence rows and the registry hardRequirements for VAPT cadence and gap closure are keyed to this parent id; the individual items are catalogued as 2.16-3.6.1.2 (annual VAPT), 2.16-3.6.1.3 (testing of changes), 2.16-3.6.1.4 (VAPT with secure code review), 2.16-3.6.1.5 (six-monthly external black-box PT), 2.16-3.6.1.9 (one-month closure of high-risk gaps) and 2.16-3.6.1.10 (two-month outer limit for all audit gaps).
evidenceExpected: VAPT and security review standard with frequency by criticality
Annual VAPT calendar
VAPT closure tracker reviewed by the IS team
ISRMC approvals for unmitigated assessment risks

controls.title: VAPT of internet-facing applications and infrastructure at least once a year
controls.prose: Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of internet-facing applications or infrastructure components shall be conducted periodically, at least once in a year.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter builds the internet-facing asset list (customer and agent portals, partner and web aggregator APIs, mobile app backends, VPN, mail gateways) and compares it with the scope of the last VAPT report; any exposed asset without a VAPT in twelve months is a finding. Import report findings via sarif-findings or ocsf-findings (checklist Q93).
evidenceExpected: VAPT reports within the last twelve months for each internet-facing asset
Reconciliation of VAPT scope to the external attack surface inventory

params.label: Minimum VAPT exercises per year for internet-facing applications and infrastructure

controls.title: Mandatory security testing of every change to internet-facing assets before production
controls.prose: Mandatory security testing shall be conducted for all changes to internet-facing information assets or systems, and reported gaps should be closed before moving into production.
controls.guidance: probe-cicd-env verifies release pipelines for internet-facing applications include DAST or targeted security test gates that block on unresolved high findings; probe-sdlc checks sdlc/policy.json ciGates reflect this. Sample recent production releases of the customer portal and APIs for security test evidence. Scope by category, Annexure II Q95 (Cat-1 Yes, Cat-2 Yes, Cat-3 "Major Changes"): insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries must evidence testing for every change to an internet-facing asset; Cat-3 intermediaries only for major changes as classified in their change procedure (2.9-3.3), so a minor untested change at a Cat-3 intermediary is not a finding. Insurers are audited against the Guidelines body and the Annexure III checklist, which has no category columns, so they take the strictest (Cat-1) value. Intermediaries take the column for their Annexure II gross-insurance-revenue category (Cat-1 >= Rs 50 crore or any ISNP or web aggregator, Cat-2 Rs 5 to 50 crore, Cat-3 < Rs 5 crore); there is no reCategory slug for this yet (see 1.4-a), so read the category from details.json regulatoryRegistrations or the latest Annexure III report and apply it manually.
evidenceExpected: Security test results attached to releases of internet-facing systems
Pipeline gates blocking release on open security gaps
Exception approvals where a release proceeded with gaps

controls.title: VAPT with secure code review for business applications, APIs and web services periodically and before go-live
controls.prose: Business applications, including APIs and web services, shall undergo security audit or VAPT testing including secure code review periodically and before go-live.
controls.guidance: execute-scr performs or ingests secure code review for proposal, underwriting, policy administration, claims, payment and partner APIs; probe-cicd-env confirms SAST results exist for the go-live commit. An application whose first production deployment predates its code review, or with no review in the assessment period, is a finding (checklist Q94).
evidenceExpected: Pre-go-live VAPT and secure code review reports per business application
Periodic API security test reports
API inventory reconciled with tested scope

controls.title: External black-box penetration test of all internet-facing assets every six months
controls.prose: External Blackbox Penetration Testing (PT) should be conducted for all internet-facing information assets and systems once in 6 months.
controls.guidance: Track external black-box PT reports covering the full external attack surface discovered by runtime-probe-network-perimeter; assets missing from the tested scope are a finding. Interval by category, Annexure II Q96 ("once in a 6 months": Cat-1 Yes, Cat-2 Yes, Cat-3 Annual): insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries at most 6 months between tests (param externalPtIntervalMonths), Cat-3 intermediaries at most 12 months (param externalPtIntervalMonthsCat3); raise a finding only when the gap exceeds the interval for the company's category. Insurers are audited against the Guidelines body and the Annexure III checklist, which has no category columns, so they take the strictest (Cat-1) value. Intermediaries take the column for their Annexure II gross-insurance-revenue category (Cat-1 >= Rs 50 crore or any ISNP or web aggregator, Cat-2 Rs 5 to 50 crore, Cat-3 < Rs 5 crore); there is no reCategory slug for this yet (see 1.4-a), so read the category from details.json regulatoryRegistrations or the latest Annexure III report and apply it manually. The clause says "should"; mandatory is kept true because the same obligation is audit checklist question Q96 in Annexures II and III, so the auditor rates a gap as a non-compliance in Part C.
evidenceExpected: External black-box penetration test reports at intervals not exceeding the category interval (6 months, or 12 months for Cat-3 intermediaries)
Scope lists covering all internet-facing assets

params.label: Maximum interval between external black-box penetration tests of internet-facing assets (insurers and Cat-1/Cat-2 intermediaries)
Maximum interval between external black-box penetration tests for Cat-3 intermediaries (Annexure II Q96: Annual)

controls.title: Close high-risk VAPT gaps within one month with validation testing
controls.prose: High risk gaps, reported from the VAPT, should be closed within a period of one month followed by validation testing.
controls.guidance: soc findings imported from VAPT with severity high or critical get slaDueAt = firstSeenAt + 30 days (slaBasis citing this control, or the 2.16-3.6.1 sla-table row) and require a revalidation observation before resolvedAt is set; refresh-soc flags breaches. slaDays 30 is the clause's one month, a remediation window stated by the clause. The clause says "should"; mandatory is kept true because the same obligation is audit checklist question Q97 in Annexures II and III (all categories "Yes"), so the auditor rates a gap as a non-compliance (checklist Q97, Q240).
evidenceExpected: VAPT tracker showing closure dates of high-risk gaps within one month
Validation or retest reports for closed gaps

params.label: Period within which high-risk VAPT gaps are closed before validation testing

controls.title: Close all audit gaps within an outer limit of two months, prioritised by risk
controls.prose: Priority for closure of audit gaps should be based on the risk associated with each gap; however, the outer time limit for closure of all the audit gaps is two months.
controls.guidance: Medium and low findings from VAPT and the annual cyber audit get slaDueAt no later than firstSeenAt + 60 days; where the sla-table sets a shorter deadline by severity, the shorter applies. Findings still open after 60 days need an ISRMC-approved soc risk acceptance (control 2.16-3.6.1) or are reported as SLA breaches. slaDays 60 is the clause's outer limit of two months. The clause says "should" for the risk-based priority; mandatory is kept true because the same obligation is audit checklist question Q98 in Annexures II and III (all categories "Yes"), so the auditor rates a gap as a non-compliance (checklist Q98).
evidenceExpected: Audit gap tracker with closure dates within two months
Risk-based prioritisation of gaps
ISRMC exception approvals for gaps beyond two months

params.label: Outer time limit for closure of all audit gaps

controls.title: Annual internal review of information security practices
controls.prose: The organisation shall conduct an annual review of information security practices, either by the IS team or by a competent independent party appointed by the IS team, to ensure compliance with the information security policies, procedures and internal standards defined by the IS team. Formal procedures shall be developed by the IS team for planning and reporting review findings and ensuring prompt and accurate remedial action.
controls.guidance: Collect the annual internal IS review report, its plan and remediation tracker; record it as a soc observation and import gaps as findings. A financial year without an internal review is a finding. External reviews are 2.16-3.6.3 and auditor rotation is 2.16-3.6.3.5.
evidenceExpected: Annual internal IS review report and remediation plan
Review planning and reporting procedure

controls.title: Formal external information security reviews by a competent independent party
controls.prose: The organisation shall conduct formal external IS reviews by a competent independent party to ensure compliance with the information security policies, procedures and external industry standards, at the frequency defined by the Information Security team. The IS team shall develop formal procedures for planning and reporting audits and audit findings and ensuring prompt and accurate remedial action, define the scope of the review and coordinate with business and support teams. Audit requirements and activities involving checks on operational systems shall be carefully planned and agreed to minimise the risk of disruption to business processes.
controls.guidance: Collect the latest external review report, its scope and the frequency set by the IS team; record the review as a soc observation and import gaps as findings. Check that audit activity on production (scans, privileged read access) was planned and approved in change_management. Item 5 of this clause (auditor rotation) is catalogued separately as 2.16-3.6.3.5; auditor eligibility is Annex-IV.
evidenceExpected: External IS review report, scope and frequency defined by the IS team
Planning and approval records for audit activities on operational systems
Remediation tracker for external review findings

controls.title: Rotate the independent assurance auditor every three years
controls.prose: Independent assurance auditor shall be rotated every three years.
controls.guidance: Store the auditor as a vendor (vendors/<vendor_id>.json, services type audit) and list the engagement letters by financial year; compute the consecutive years the same audit firm has certified the annual assurance audit (1.10-a) and raise a finding when a fourth consecutive year is engaged. Eligibility of the firm is Annex-IV.
evidenceExpected: Engagement letters by financial year showing the audit firm
Rotation plan naming the next eligible firm

params.label: Maximum consecutive years before the independent assurance auditor is rotated

controls.title: Register of legal, regulatory and contractual requirements mapped to controls
controls.prose: All relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements, including local ones, and the organisation's approach to meeting them shall be explicitly identified, documented and kept up to date, with statute-backed regulations made compulsory and formal risk analysis used to select the controls regulators and laws require. Legal advice shall be sought on requirements, the CISO shall document them in a register with the associated controls, the legal department shall instruct employees and review compliance regularly, and procedures shall protect intellectual property rights and proprietary software licences. The organisation shall adhere to all applicable IRDAI circulars and incorporate them in operations, protect customer data confidentiality under the IT Act 2000 as amended in 2008, devise procedures for amendments and new cyber or privacy laws, and adhere to the Aadhaar Act, rules and amendments. Annexure A lists the IT (Amendment) Act 2008, Companies Act, Insurance Act, IRDAI regulations, Contract Act, FEMA, Stamp Act, personnel laws, data privacy law and the Aadhaar Act.
controls.guidance: details.json frameworksInScope is the machine register: for an insurer or intermediary it must include irdai-info-cyber-security-2023, cert-in-directions-2022, dpdp-act-2023 and dpdp-rules-2025; refresh-ctx flags missing instruments and new IRDAI circulars. Evidence the CISO's compliance register mapping each requirement to controls and owners, and Aadhaar vault or tokenisation controls where Aadhaar numbers are processed for e-KYC.
evidenceExpected: Compliance register of legal, regulatory and contractual requirements with mapped controls
Tracker of IRDAI circulars and their implementation
Aadhaar data handling controls where applicable
Software licence compliance records

controls.title: Cyber threat intelligence process and participation in information-sharing groups
controls.prose: The organisation shall establish and follow a cyber threat intelligence, analysis and information-sharing process. It shall identify cyber threats that could affect operational performance, significantly impact its objectives and obligations, or threaten critical business processes and reputation; gather and analyse threat information together with internal and external business and system information; actively participate in information-sharing groups to receive and share indicators relating to cyber incidents; and regularly send cyber security awareness circulars and advisories to employees, third-party vendors and consultants.
controls.guidance: Evidence threat intelligence feeds in use (CERT-In advisories, CSIRT-Fin, NCIIPC alerts, sector ISAC or vendor feeds), how indicators are ingested into the SIEM or EDR, membership of information-sharing groups and the advisory circulars issued. cve-enrichment records CERT-In advisory references on CVE records used by findings.
evidenceExpected: Threat intelligence process document and feed subscriptions
Membership or participation records for information-sharing groups
Indicator ingestion into SIEM or EDR
Awareness advisories sent to employees and vendors

controls.title: Cyber Crisis Management Plan with information-sharing arrangements, rehearsed periodically
controls.prose: A plan shall define information sharing through trusted channels when an incident occurs as part of the response programme. Information-sharing arrangements shall be documented in a Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) for large incidents to facilitate sector-wide response, and CERT-In or NCIIPC guidelines may be used to prepare the CCMP. The audit checklist asks whether a CCMP is available and prepared using CERT-In or NCIIPC guidelines and whether the cyber crisis plan is implemented and exercised or rehearsed periodically.
controls.guidance: Collect the CCMP (version, approval, scenarios such as ransomware on the policy administration system, policyholder data leak, DDoS on the customer portal), its communication tree covering IRDAI, CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin and media, and the last tabletop or crisis simulation report with actions tracked in change_management. No rehearsal in the last twelve months is a finding (checklist Q125, Q255).
evidenceExpected: Approved Cyber Crisis Management Plan aligned to CERT-In or NCIIPC guidance
Crisis communication and information-sharing tree
Tabletop or crisis simulation reports with action tracking

controls.title: Risk-based cloud adoption and approval of mandatory controls before contract signature
controls.prose: Cloud services shall meet business and security requirements and relevant laws across provisioning, operations and decommissioning. Cloud adoption decisions shall evaluate technical adequacy of porting the application, risk including availability, regulatory, compliance, statutory and data-sensitivity requirements, and control over intrusion decisions, vulnerability monitoring and denial of service. Assets moving to cloud shall be evaluated for importance and for the impact of disclosure, CSP insider access, manipulation, failure, unexpected change and unavailability. The organisation shall comply with IRDAI guidelines and Indian laws and ensure all mandatory controls are approved before signing an agreement with the cloud service provider. Deviations follow risk and exception management.
controls.guidance: Evidence cloud adoption risk assessments per workload (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, BPaaS) dated before contract signature, and the mandatory control checklist sign-off. refresh-vendor-ctx records each CSP in vendors/ with services type cloud, criticality and hostingCountries; applications/<app_id>/env hosting.provider must match a vendor with a completed assessment (checklist Q133).
evidenceExpected: Cloud adoption risk assessment per workload
Mandatory cloud control checklist approved before contract signature
CSP vendor records with service model and hosting countries

controls.title: Secure cloud infrastructure baseline, pre-rollout assessment and cloud IAM
controls.prose: The cloud environment shall be designed on security guidelines such as the Cloud Security Alliance Cloud Controls Matrix or IS-team guidelines, with the IS team assessing private cloud services before rollout. An infrastructure standard including a minimum security baseline shall govern commissioning of cloud servers and network equipment; tools shall monitor storage, allocation, uptime, response times, patching, change, incident and antivirus management; applications and infrastructure shall be evaluated for cloud suitability and security baseline before migration under a documented procedure with security and business approvals; and cloud infrastructure shall follow the information systems maintenance policy. The CSP shall support multi-factor authentication and its authentication, access control, accountability and logging shall meet regulatory and legal requirements, and the CSP shall have documented, tested processes for network access control, firewall filtering, VPN, IDS or IPS, DDoS mitigation and logging with notification.
controls.guidance: probe-iac evaluates Terraform, CloudFormation or Bicep against a CSA CCM or CIS cloud benchmark baseline (root or owner account MFA, no long-lived access keys, organisation guardrails, flow logs, GuardDuty or Defender equivalents, DDoS protection on public endpoints); runtime-probe-prod-env and runtime-probe-identity-access verify the running cloud posture read-only. Evidence migration approvals for workloads moved to cloud.
evidenceExpected: Cloud security baseline mapped to CSA CCM or CIS benchmarks
Cloud posture management reports
MFA enforcement for cloud console and API access
DDoS protection and flow log configuration
Migration security approvals

controls.title: Tenant data isolation and dedicated encryption keys in the cloud
controls.prose: The organisation's cloud data shall be isolated so it can operate as a separately managed entity, with isolation at network, operating system, application and database layers; in multi-tenant environments storage, memory and routing usage shall be separated, data segregated into its own database instance in isolated architectures, and privacy across tenants enforced through access control where native multi-tenancy is used, with business and technical errors logged separately. Cryptographic controls shall follow data classification with a unique set of encryption keys; the CSP shall support KMIP, hardware-backed keys compliant with FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 are preferred where compatible, and procedures shall cover encryption in transit, at rest and on backup media, secure and access-limited key stores, key protection, standards-based encryption, key backup and recoverability, and testing of these procedures.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks that data stores holding policyholder data use customer-managed keys dedicated to the company (not provider-default keys), HSM-backed where available, with key policies restricted to named roles; for SaaS multi-tenant platforms (CRM, claims SaaS) refresh-vendor-ctx collects tenant isolation and key management attestations. probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-prod-env check Kubernetes namespace and network isolation for multi-entity group platforms.
evidenceExpected: Customer-managed, dedicated encryption keys for cloud data stores
HSM or FIPS 140-2/140-3 validation evidence for key storage
Tenant isolation design or SaaS provider attestation
Key backup and recovery test records

controls.title: Cloud offboarding with data return, deletion evidence and decommissioning certificate
controls.prose: On termination, all data transferred by or generated for the organisation shall be handed over to it, the CSP shall provide evidence of deletion and purging of all copies at its sites, data in transit shall be protected per classification, and the CSP shall certify that decommissioning is complete and no further access remains. The CSP's disaster recovery plan shall be audited to confirm data retrieval after loss, provision of DR test reports, equal security in DR mode and CSP ownership of the DR solution, with continuity provisions included in contracts.
controls.guidance: For cloud vendors moving to status terminated, refresh-vendor-ctx requires a deletion or decommissioning certificate in assurance evidence, and probe-iac confirms residual resources, keys and cross-account roles are removed. Collect CSP DR test reports annually for active providers.
evidenceExpected: Data handover records at cloud exit
CSP deletion and decommissioning certificates
CSP DR test reports

controls.title: Virtualisation and image security: hardened VMs, authorised snapshots, hypervisor logs, CSP sub-vendor list
controls.prose: The organisation shall evaluate the CSP's virtualisation hardening guidelines against its technology risk assessment checklist, including disabling unnecessary interfaces, ports and services, securing virtual network interfaces and storage, limiting VM resource usage, hardening operating systems, applications, VM virtual hardware and containers, and validating cryptographic key-management integrity. The CSP shall ensure only authorised snapshots and images are taken with classification, storage location and encryption consistent with production, provide access to hypervisor administrative access logs with complete hypervisor logging, provide trusted hardened VMs, and give and keep current the complete list of its vendors with access to the organisation's data. Applications shall be qualified on the deployed virtualisation product and VM resources monitored against load.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks machine images and snapshots are encrypted and not shared publicly or cross-account without approval; probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers check container hardening (non-root, seccomp, no privileged pods, minimal base images, signed images); runtime-probe-sandboxes checks isolation of code-execution sandboxes. refresh-vendor-ctx records CSP subcontractors in vendors/<vendor_id>.json services[].subcontractors.
evidenceExpected: VM and container hardening standard and compliance results
Snapshot and image sharing and encryption configuration
Hypervisor or cloud control-plane administrative access logs
CSP sub-processor list with change notifications

controls.title: Cloud contract: data ownership, no secondary use, breach notice within 4 hours, SLAs and exit
controls.prose: An NDA shall be signed with the CSP before service, and a service contract shall address the architectural framework, governance and risk management, CSP and organisation roles, e-discovery, expert testimony, primary data and logs, storage location, termination and data ownership, with the right to audit (CSA STAR-certified providers with in-scope services may furnish a self-certificate and certificate instead of periodic audits). SLAs shall reflect application and data availability requirements during planned and unplanned outages, BCP, DR, backup and redundancy, with financial remedies for disruption, automated SLA tracking and contracts approved by Legal with Compliance, Risk and IS. The organisation shall retain exclusive ownership of all data copies including backups, prohibit CSP use for advertising or secondary purposes, be informed of any confirmed breach immediately and of a suspected breach within 4 hours of discovery, hold the CSP liable for losses and penalties from its breach, and require complete data elimination, media sanitisation, return of data and no vendor lock-in at termination.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx checks CSP and SaaS contracts for the listed clauses and records gaps as findings against the vendor: breach notification longer than 4 hours for suspected breaches, missing data return and deletion, missing storage location commitment or no financial remedy. Where standard hyperscaler terms cannot be negotiated, record an approved exception with compensating controls (customer-managed keys, own backups).
evidenceExpected: Cloud contract and DPA clauses on data ownership, secondary use and liability
Breach notification clause with 4-hour suspected breach timeline
Availability SLA with financial remedies
Exit and data return and deletion clauses
NDA with the CSP

params.label: Hours from discovery within which the CSP informs the organisation of a suspected breach

controls.title: Regulator access to cloud infrastructure and compliance with Indian law
controls.prose: The organisation shall ensure the CSP's data privacy policy complies with applicable laws and that the CSP adheres to all regulatory and legal requirements of India, with data and processes in the cloud complying with both Indian and international laws where the organisation has an international presence. It shall contractually agree with the CSP that infrastructure and applications are available for audit and inspection by the country's regulators, giving the regulator access to all information resources consumed by the organisation even though they are not physically on its premises. (The Guidelines number these paragraphs 5.7.3 and 5.7.4 within policy 2.19.)
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx checks every CSP and material SaaS contract for an explicit regulator (IRDAI) audit and inspection clause and records contract.rightToAudit; absence for a vendor supporting a critical function is a high finding. Also evaluate Annex-III.146 data localisation for the same vendors.
evidenceExpected: Contract clause granting IRDAI and other Indian regulators audit and inspection access
CSP privacy policy review against Indian law

controls.title: Cyber resilience programme with classification of critical systems and incidents
controls.prose: Critical systems and cyber security incidents shall be classified by criticality and severity, with an incident classification guideline defined in the incident management procedure. A cyber security management programme consistent with cyber resilience best practice shall be in place and verified through supervisory review, covering identification (threats, critical assets and functions, sensitive personal information, vendor and process risk), protection (controls by technical standards, resilience by design, least-privilege access, the human factor), detection through security monitoring of critical systems, response and recovery with periodically tested contingency plans, testing through VAPT at different stages of development and maintenance, learning and reporting (continual re-evaluation and reporting incidents that compromise critical information to regulators within their timelines), and situational awareness through information sharing and regular advisories. Forensic investigations may be performed for incidents with legal, regulatory or severe impact, handling digital evidence per law.
controls.guidance: Check details.json criticalFunctions and the per-application tier in applications/<app_id>/env/<env_id>.json cover all critical systems, and that the incident classification guideline maps to soc severity. report-audit-improvements summarises resilience programme initiatives from change_management. Forensics is permissive ("may"); record forensic retainer or capability as an observation rather than a gap.
evidenceExpected: Critical system classification register
Incident classification guideline
Cyber resilience programme plan and supervisory review results
Forensic investigation capability or retainer

controls.title: DMARC with SPF and DKIM, DNS filtering, attachment sandboxing and macro control
controls.prose: Formal transfer policies, procedures and controls should be in place to protect information transferred through email, voice, fax, video and software downloads. To lower the chance of spoofed or modified email from valid domains the organisation shall implement DMARC policy and verification, starting with SPF and DKIM. DNS filtering services shall block access to known malicious domains, sandboxing shall analyse and block inbound attachments with malicious behaviour, and measures shall control VBA macros in Office documents and permissible attachment types. The audit checklist also expects secure mail systems for partners and vendors preventing spoofing and look-alike domains.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter resolves SPF, DKIM selectors and DMARC for every sending domain in details.json website and brand domains, flagging missing records, p=none policies, SPF with +all or more than ten lookups, and look-alike domains used for policyholder communication. Evidence email gateway sandboxing, attachment-type blocking and macro policy (checklist Q12, Q68, Q76, Q78, Q86, Q215).
evidenceExpected: DNS records showing SPF, DKIM and DMARC at enforcement
DMARC aggregate report monitoring
Email gateway sandboxing and attachment filtering configuration
DNS filtering service configuration
Office macro control policy

controls.title: Board-approved policy addressing work-from-remote-location risks
controls.prose: The Board-approved Cyber Security Policy shall address work from remote location (WFRL) risks and mandate frequent password changes. Workflow approvals, deviations and exceptions shall be captured under change control; audit log monitoring and analysis shall be provisioned on organisational ICT infrastructure as a control for unauthorised access and cyber threats; evidence and artefacts shall be classified and not shared outside authorised domains; project documents and MIS reports shared on need-to-know basis; and IT support for investment application users available through portal, helpdesk, email or office visit during disruption.
controls.guidance: Evidence the WFRL section of the Board-approved policy and its approval date; the remaining WFRL technical obligations are evaluated under 2.22-3.2 and 2.22-3.3 (checklist Q256, Q258, Q265, Q267).
evidenceExpected: Board-approved policy section on WFRL risks
Password change requirement for remote users
Audit log monitoring coverage for remote access

controls.title: Hardened, monitored remote endpoints with VPN or VDI-only access
controls.prose: For remote working the organisation shall ensure secure networks with strong protocols and Wi-Fi passwords; provide authorised assets hardened per security policy with strong authentication; harden servers, applications and networks; implement device controls blocking unauthorised internet domains, admin-level access, unauthorised software installation or changes, USB and other media and peripherals; enable antivirus, endpoint protection, data encryption and DLP on all user systems and check they function; regularly patch user systems and ICT infrastructure, including to prevent DDoS; provision VPN, internet proxy or VDI for remote users and make applications accessible only to authorised users over secured VPN; scan systems brought back to office; detect unauthorised access, malicious code, suspicious behaviour, credential theft and remote access toolkits; secure email against spam, spoofing and malware with phishing training; block malicious domains at firewall, proxy and IPS; and perform DR drills to confirm business continuity metrics.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks that internal applications are reachable only via VPN, ZTNA or VDI with MFA and device posture; probe-dev-env checks developer laptops and cloud workstations for disk encryption, EDR, USB control and local admin restrictions; runtime-probe-network-perimeter confirms internal admin applications are not exposed directly to the internet. Evidence EDR and DLP coverage for remote endpoints (checklist Q259 to Q264, Q266, Q273, Q276).
evidenceExpected: Endpoint compliance report (encryption, EDR, DLP, patch level) for remote users
Device control and local admin restriction policies
VPN, ZTNA or VDI configuration restricting application access
Detection rules for remote access toolkits and credential theft

controls.title: Remote data protection, NDAs before remote operations and privileged access audit
controls.prose: While remote working is permitted, data containerisation, multi-factor authentication and remote wipe shall prevent tampering and misuse of lost mobile devices; users shall back up critical data periodically to secure organisation locations with backups reviewed; non-disclosure agreements or undertakings on data security and confidentiality shall be signed by employees, consultants and vendors before remote operations commence; controls for secure access from BYOD devices shall be defined; privileged user identity and access authentication shall be audited; and audit walkthroughs and interviews shall use approved remote access software over secure, hardened systems.
controls.guidance: Evidence app-protection or containerisation policy, NDA signature dates before remote access grant dates for vendor staff (runtime-probe-identity-access provides grant dates), privileged access audit reports and the approved remote collaboration tool list (checklist Q269 to Q272, Q274, Q275).
evidenceExpected: Mobile app-protection and remote wipe policy
NDAs dated before remote access provisioning
Privileged remote access audit report
Approved remote audit and collaboration tools

controls.title: Recorded, authorised and resilient dealing room operations for investment functions
controls.prose: A dealing room operation procedure should be developed. Dealers shall execute all transactions only through recorded telephone lines, authorised Bloomberg terminals or Bloomberg Anywhere IDs, NDS or TREPS terminals or authorised email, with a dedicated secure recording line when working from home; recorded lines shall be maintained, calls from office recorded on a voice logger with backups retained as proof of transaction, and communications between dealers and brokers logged and independently reviewed by the mid-office. Orders shall be placed only with empanelled brokers via authorised modes, with prior approvals per the dealing room workflow, email only from registered company addresses, SMS and chat disabled on Bloomberg terminals and MFA enabled on them, and a supervisory checklist covering price and trade monitoring with regular voice recording analysis and rate scans. Procedures shall handle communication disruptions, secondary connectivity shall be provisioned and tested, and DR drills and contingency plans for the investment function tested periodically with issues documented.
controls.guidance: Applies to insurers with an in-house investment function. Evidence voice logger configuration and retention, mid-office review logs, Bloomberg terminal MFA and chat-disable settings, empanelled broker list and the investment function DR drill report; record as manual-method observations (audit checklist WFRL.IN area, questions under Work From Remote Location Investment).
evidenceExpected: Dealing room SOP and authorisation matrix
Voice logger recording and retention evidence
Mid-office review logs of dealer communications
Bloomberg terminal MFA and chat-disable configuration
Investment function DR drill report

groups.title: 2.24 Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021

controls.title: Publish prohibited-content rules and remind users at least once a year
controls.prose: The organisation's rules and regulations, privacy policy or user agreement shall inform users of its computer resources not to host, display, upload, modify, publish, transmit, store, update or share information that belongs to another person without right; is defamatory, obscene, invasive of privacy, harassing, racially objectionable or relates to money laundering or gambling; is harmful to children; infringes intellectual property; violates any law; deceives about origin or is patently false; impersonates another person; threatens the unity, integrity, security or sovereignty of India or public order; contains malicious code; or is false and published to mislead or harass for gain. At least once a year it shall inform users of its rules, privacy policy or user agreement and any changes, and that non-compliance may lead to immediate termination of access or removal of content. It shall not host unlawful information after actual knowledge through a court order or government notification, and shall not knowingly change the normal course of operation of a computer resource to circumvent law.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter fetches the terms of use and privacy policy from customer portals and apps (for web aggregators, ISNPs and insurer portals) and checks for the prohibited-content clause; evidence the annual user notification (email or in-app) dated within twelve months (checklist Q337 to Q340, Q345).
evidenceExpected: Published terms of use and privacy policy with prohibited-content clauses
Annual user notification records
Takedown records for court or government orders

controls.title: Provide information or assistance to authorised government agencies within 72 hours of an order
controls.prose: The organisation shall, as soon as possible and not later than seventy-two hours after receipt of an order, provide information under its control or possession, or assistance, to a government agency lawfully authorised for investigative, protective or cyber security activities, for identity verification or the prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of offences or for cyber security incidents. It shall report cyber security incidents and share related information with CERT-In under the CERT-In Rules 2013, and take reasonable security measures under the IT (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Information) Rules 2011.
controls.guidance: Evidence the law enforcement request procedure with a named nodal officer, a log of orders with receipt and response timestamps, and log retention adequate to answer requests (see 2.16-3.3.14). A response beyond 72 hours is a finding. No slaDays: 72 hours (param governmentOrderResponseHours) is the time to answer each order, not a remediation period, so a finding against this control takes its deadline from the SLA table by severity.
evidenceExpected: Government and law enforcement request handling procedure
Register of orders with receipt and response times within 72 hours

params.label: Hours from receipt of an order within which information or assistance is provided

controls.title: Grievance Officer published; acknowledge complaints in 24 hours and resolve in 15 days
controls.prose: The organisation shall publish on its website, mobile application or both the name and contact details of its Grievance Officer and the mechanism for users or victims to complain about violations or other matters concerning its computer resources. The Grievance Officer shall acknowledge complaints within twenty-four hours and dispose of them within fifteen days of receipt, and receive and acknowledge orders, notices or directions from the Government, competent authorities or courts. Where a complaint concerns content exposing an individual's private areas, showing nudity or sexual acts, or impersonation including morphed images, the organisation shall within twenty-four hours take reasonable measures to remove or disable access, and provide a mechanism for such complaints. User registration information shall be retained for one hundred and eighty days after cancellation or withdrawal of registration.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks customer websites and app store listings for the Grievance Officer name, contact and complaint mechanism. Evidence the grievance register with acknowledgement and closure timestamps against 24 hours and 15 days, and data retention settings keeping deregistered user records for 180 days (checklist Q341, Q346 to Q348). No slaDays: 24 hours and 15 days (params grievanceAckHours, grievanceDisposalDays) are handling times for each complaint, not a remediation period, so a finding such as a missing grievance mechanism takes its deadline from the SLA table by severity.
evidenceExpected: Published Grievance Officer details and complaint mechanism
Grievance register with acknowledgement within 24 hours and disposal within 15 days
Takedown records within 24 hours for intimate or impersonation content complaints
Retention configuration for deregistered user records (180 days)

params.label: Hours within which the Grievance Officer acknowledges a complaint
Days within which a complaint is disposed of
Days user registration information is retained after cancellation or withdrawal

groups.title: Circular IRDAI/GA&HR/CIR/MISC/128/06/2023 (13 June 2023): Reporting of cyber security incidents by regulated entities

controls.title: Submit incident details to IRDAI in the prescribed format within 24 hours
controls.prose: Noting that regulated entities were not adhering to the 6-hour CERT-In timeline or keeping the Authority in the loop, IRDAI directed all regulated entities to scrupulously follow the incident reporting provisions of para 3.5 of policy 2.10 and, further, to submit the available details of a cyber security incident to the Authority in the enclosed reporting format within 24 hours of intimation of the incident.
controls.guidance: Add an IRDAI regulatorReportRefs entry with deadlineHours 24 on every reportable soc incident, separate from the 6-hour CERT-In copy. The enclosed reporting format was not available in this extraction and the circular was read from a PDF copy rather than a fetched IRDAI URL; maintainer verification needed for the format fields and the circular's IRDAI URL. No slaDays: 24 hours (param irdaiReportingHours) is a reporting window for each incident, not a remediation period; a finding about a missing reporting procedure takes its deadline from the SLA table by severity.
evidenceExpected: IRDAI incident reporting format submissions with timestamps within 24 hours of intimation
Mapping of incident register fields to the IRDAI format

params.label: Hours from intimation of the incident within which details are submitted to IRDAI in the prescribed format

controls.title: Submit updated incident report versions to IRDAI within 24 hours of new forensic information
controls.prose: The details in the IRDAI incident reporting format shall be updated as forensic analysis yields information and submitted to the Authority as subsequent versions within 24 hours of such information becoming available.
controls.guidance: Record each forensic update in the soc incident timeline and a further IRDAI regulatorReportRefs entry (reference with version suffix) submitted within 24 hours of the timeline entry; refresh-soc flags timeline entries tagged forensic without a follow-up submission. Maintainer verification needed for the circular's IRDAI URL. No slaDays: 24 hours is a reporting window for each forensic update, not a remediation period.
evidenceExpected: Versioned IRDAI incident report submissions
Forensic report milestones with dates
Submission timestamps within 24 hours of each forensic update

groups.title: Annexure III: Auditor's report and audit checklist (obligations stated only in the checklist)

controls.title: API-based operations and monetary transactions follow international standards
controls.prose: The audit checklist (question 123, Governance) asks whether operations, processes or monetary transactions implemented through APIs follow best practices from international standards such as ISO 27001 or COBIT 5, and whether those practices are periodically reviewed. The checklist also asks whether third parties connecting through APIs or EDI are treated under the Annexure I category requiring all sub-chapters.
controls.guidance: execute-scr and runtime-probe-network-perimeter assess partner, web aggregator, bancassurance and payment APIs for authentication (mTLS or OAuth client credentials), authorisation per partner, rate limiting, input validation and logging; map results to OWASP API guidance recorded as observations. Evidence an API security standard and its periodic review. Maintainer verification: checklist wording extracted from PDF text.
evidenceExpected: API security standard referencing international frameworks
API inventory with partner authentication method
Periodic API security review records

controls.title: ICT infrastructure, critical and business data stored in India
controls.prose: The Annexure III audit checklist question 146, under Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control (PR.AC), asks: "Are ICT infrastructure, Critical and Business data stored in India?". The Annexure II version of the same question reads "Are ICT infrastructure logs, Critical and Business data stored in India?" (Cat-1, Cat-2 and Cat-3: Yes). A negative answer is reported as a non-compliance with a risk rating in Part C of the auditor's report.
controls.guidance: This obligation appears in the audit checklist rather than the body of the Guidelines, so auditors rate it as a control; mandatory is set on that basis. The id follows the Annexure III wording (data stores); the Annexure II wording adds ICT infrastructure logs, which are covered by 2.16-3.3.14 (180-day retention within India, checklist Q145). probe-iac and runtime-probe-datapipeline check hosting regions of databases, object stores, backups, analytics warehouses and DR sites against Indian regions; refresh-vendor-ctx checks hostingCountries for SaaS processors of policyholder data (CRM, call recording, claims analytics). Any critical or business data store outside India is a high finding unless a documented regulatory permission exists. The id "Annex-III.146" was assigned during extraction from the annexure and question number.
evidenceExpected: Region inventory of production, DR and backup data stores
SaaS and vendor hosting country declarations
Architecture evidence that critical and business data remain in India

groups.title: Annexure IV: Eligibility criteria for the audit firm

controls.title: Engage an eligible, independent auditor that performs substantive testing
controls.prose: The cyber security auditor shall be either a Chartered Accountant partnership or LLP registered with ICAI with at least five years of continuous practice and at least four partners, of whom at least one is CISA or DISA certified, one is a Fellow of ICAI, one has three years of cyber or information security audit experience with insurers, banks or mutual funds, and one has IT-environment and remote audit experience; or a CERT-In empanelled external systems auditor holding CISA or DISA. The auditor must not be banned or declared ineligible by the Government, IRDAI, SEBI, RBI, ICAI, CERT-In, SFIO or any regulator, nor face pending disciplinary proceedings. Certification does not recognise management representations or reliance on other auditors' work; the auditor shall test through interviews, document verification, compliance and substantive checks and keep working papers for the Authority. Before issuing the engagement letter the entity shall obtain the auditor's eligibility declaration and retain it with the engagement letter.
controls.guidance: Store the auditor as a vendor (vendors/<vendor_id>.json, services type audit) with assurance evidence of eligibility: partner certifications or CERT-In empanelment reference, the declaration and engagement letter dates. Findings relying on management representation should be re-tested. Auditor rotation every three years is printed in policy 2.16 clause 3.6.3 item 5 and is catalogued as 2.16-3.6.3.5. The group and control ids "Annexure-IV" and "Annex-IV" are not printed labels; they were assigned during extraction for the annexure as a whole.
evidenceExpected: Auditor eligibility declaration obtained before the engagement letter
Partner qualifications (CISA/DISA, FCA, cyber audit experience) or CERT-In empanelment proof
Auditor working papers showing interviews, document verification and substantive testing
